Tarn’s ear-sentence stopped at the calling word in an ended term with the loan uncalled and Jorra’s promise ungiven against the burned slate at five; the hand outside the wool came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing and came down flat on answer 450 as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking; four readings now stand behind one unsigned figure, four being four and not one account, the first not made a thirteenth by the three that follow, the second supplying no signature, the third no doctrine, the fourth no payer, the twelve of Y.H. 813 not laid across the four, the figure read still not the figure paid; he still cannot close two inches to the pot handle, lift the crust or speak a number; died 2024, Chicago, in a fire after a blizzard (first life)}\CRfield{First seen}{Chapter 1}}{\CRsheetheading{Appearance}
In the old life he was a large man gone soft in the middle, with forearms like a butcher’s and a left knee that clicked when the weather turned. His hands were short-fingered and steady, with a pale line where a wedding ring had been; his hair went early at the temples, and on post-call days he shaved badly and did not care. He smelled of hand sanitiser, machine coffee and the faint metallic tang of a hospital cleaned too many times with the same mop. People read his face as anger. It was fatigue, and he never corrected them, because correcting them cost something.

In the new life all of that is folded into an infant body that cannot hold up its own head. The surgeon’s hands are now small soft wrists with milky nails; the butcher’s forearms are gone; the clicking knee is a soft unformed joint that will click again in time. Across his ribs and down his forearm runs a branching red mark like a frost-flower or a burn map, which the midwife Alda Reed crossed herself at and called a birth-flower, and which is in truth the fire writing itself into the hot trace that crossed with him. He drools. He cannot turn over. He is washed, dressed and discussed in the third person by people who do not know there is a forty-year-old man listening. He is a trauma surgeon who cannot reach a cup. He counts the nails in the floorboards because there is nothing else to count, four on the near board, four on the next, and a fifth that is not a nail but a knot the width of a thumb.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
He speaks little, plainly, low, and exactly. His question is usually the shortest one in the room. He does not use the old-life idiom with people who would find it strange; he never says \emph{I was a surgeon once}, because no words in Grath would carry it. With the few adults who can bear it, the Chicago rhythm comes back: faster, profane, warm under the withering. Under danger his sentences get shorter, not longer, and the clinical register takes over completely.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “How long since he stopped moving? Not the story. How long.”

\item “I’m not asking you to pray. Hand me the clamp.”

\item “That’s a lovely account. Shame nobody’s holding the heat.”

\item “Leave it. It’s gone.” — the sentence that is his gift and his heresy in Sarn.

\item “Don’t set that down. You’ll pay for it in the thaw.” — learned from the clay yard, said in the local proverb-form before he has fully learned to mean it.

\item Remembered, in the old life: \emph{You’re back on in ten, Marchetti.} said in a voice like a file.

\item Ch 7: he has learned to find the joke funny without laughing --- a way of laughing that costs less and keeps the same blade in it. He keeps the count in loaves and glances, in the kiln’s four, four and a gap, and in the space where a fifth thing should be, and tells nobody what it counts.

\end{itemize}

He cannot stop reading bodies. At a family dinner he noticed a new knuckle on his brother’s hand and a cut his aunt wiped on her skirt before anyone saw. He counts without deciding to: pulses per ten seconds, exits in any room, steps from the bed to the door. His humour is fast and withering and used like a handrail. He finishes everything on his plate, including food he dislikes, because waste offends him in a way he cannot explain.

\CRsheetheading{History}
He was born in 1984 and raised in a two-storey brick bungalow in Hermosa, on a block where the el ran high and iron over Pulaski and the summer smelled of charcoal and wet pavement. His father Aldo was a machinist from near Bari who showed love by fixing things and never learned to say it; his mother Theresa worked as a nurse’s aide and came home smelling of bleach and lilac soap. There were three children: Dan, Jimmy the patrol officer, and Lisa who left for Florida. The house was loud and full and he learned from it volume, profanity, the duty of finishing everything on his plate, and the certainty that love is a practical act refused in conversation. He went to Lane Tech because his mother insisted, took things apart on the shop floor, and found the human body in the cadaver lab at the University of Illinois Chicago the way other boys find engines: by being forbidden and doing it anyway. Anatomy did not argue. It had a right answer under your hands.

He trained at Cook County, became an attending, worked nights because nights paid more and days were when the administration was awake. What he knew, precisely: airway in blood and dark, a cricothyrotomy with a knife and tube if the mouth was destroyed; the difference between pulsing blood and welling blood, packing a cavity, the third rib that tears the lung; reducing shoulders and pinning femurs; burns by the rule of nines and the Parkland formula; hypothermia the way a priest knows sin — the afterdrop, the fact that a cold patient cannot clot, that the grimace of severe cold looks like a smile, that you do not rub a frozen foot; sterile field, debridement, leaving a wound open; the small evidence a body carries; and above all triage, the ninety-second sorting of twenty injured people into those who will live, those who will live only if he chooses them, and those who will die whatever he does. He did it hundreds of times and never once found a way to make it feel clean.

What he did not know mattered as much. He was a clinician, not a physicist. He could not grow penicillin, anaesthetise with a weed, make a fire with his hands, track a beast, bargain for food, read a Sarnish ledger, or make a native believe a clamped vessel might survive. He was an amateur boxer from his twenties — enough to keep his chin down and take one punch and wait. He knew exactly how a body fails and was almost helpless when the body in question was his own.

He married Elena Rossi in 2007; their daughter Nina was born in 2000. The shifts ate the marriage. He was absent for the dinners and the small ordinary evenings that turn out to be the whole of a life. The divorce was quiet and worse for it. He kept a photograph of Nina at six on his wall and looked at it every night without seeing it. There was Marisol Vega after, an emergency-room nurse kind enough to try for eleven months, who left because she was tired of being the woman who waits. There was Des Carter, who made jokes instead of asking; Ostrowski, who taught him to decide and carry; Vesci, who called him the butcher and never forgave the report.

When he was thirty-one a twenty-two-year-old named Tasha Broussard came in after a fight, was examined, had a normal blood pressure and a bruised abdomen, and was discharged with a sprain. She returned four hours later in cardiac arrest from a ruptured spleen the size of a fist. The junior had missed the sign; Dan, covering the shift, signed the chart without reading the nurse’s note that said she had been vomiting. At the review he let the hospital call it a systems failure and said nothing about the note. He kept his job, his licence and his reputation, and carried the shape of his own conduct for the rest of his life. His father died that spring while Dan was on a thirty-six-hour shift; he noticed the casket was slightly crooked in the aisle and thought about it for years.

He died in February, in a blizzard, on the expressway at 2:17 in the morning, going back to the minivan for the last time and getting the child out before the fire took the van and took him. His phone was lit in his coat with a name he would not look at. The last thing he knew, orderless: the hiss of fuel, the orange light on snow, the cold leaving his hands, and a wordless sentence that was nevertheless complete — \emph{I have left the job unfinished.} A woman in a coat the colour of wet ash stood at the edge of the flare light writing on a slate, and her writing did not stop.

He woke as an infant in Low Kiln, taken in by Sella Vail of the kiln-house, with the birth-flower across his ribs and a warm stone at his belly that was already going cold.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
The body’s humiliations are exact: drool, the useless head, the blanket that will not stay on, the small animal sound that comes when he turns his head past a point, the cup two paces off that he cannot reach. Day 1 is lived awake from the birth to morning; nobody thinks to ask whether he wants to be awake. By the afternoon of Day 3, under the Vail roof, heat has come back into his hands and feet with the itch and sting of a rewarming, which he reads in reverse; the pale stone that held the last of that warmth was left in the fold of grey wool in House Silt, and he feels the place of it as an empty place felt with an exactness that has nothing to do with temperature. But the deeper wounds are old ones. The missed call to Nina, promising a boat on Lake Michigan for nine years. Tasha’s chart and the note he did not read. The crooked casket nobody corrected. A sister in Florida, a mother’s kitchen, a father who could not say what he felt and so fixed things.

He fears being the only adult in the room and him with the hands of a child. He fears that his clinical gift is not a gift at all but a moral defect — that the willingness to say \emph{leave it} says something about him he would rather not know. He fears the hollow and the Kept: a vessel that holds perfectly and feels nothing, which is the thing he has spent his life doing to himself in the name of duty. He fears going home most of all, because the mechanism is real and the price is the warmth of the woman the child in the minivan became. He cannot pay that account by dying again; it can only be carried.

His contradictions are the engine of him. He who decided who was beyond saving now lives in a world whose founding doctrine is that nobody is ever beyond keeping. He who fled intimacy now carries a whole district’s debt. He distrusts institutions because he has performed their gesture himself — and yet he learns their trades, joins a household, and will one day wear the Court’s own disciplines like a skin. He is most himself when he is least comfortable, which is a dangerous thing to be in a world where comfort is stolen from the poor and he will not notice that somebody else is paying for his.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wants to go home. He wants to hear Nina’s voice, to say the nine-year-old sentence about the lake and the boat, to put down the phone he keeps reaching for in a pocket that holds nothing. He thinks he wants a better clamp: a way to mend the world’s crack without spending anyone, a way to pay the debt of the Forty of Low Kiln whose warmth bought his whole return. What he needs is harder and he will spend thousands of chapters arriving at it: that repair is not restoration, that a mended vessel carries its break, that a debt can be carried instead of settled, that attention is the one thing no institution can tax, and that the answer is not a tighter seal but a third thing — a repair that leaves the crack visible and the Warm free to move.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Ch 128 (bonds).} Across Silt 11, 12 and 13 nothing crossed under the Vail roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the second asking at the well on the twelfth nor the Slate Row face at the yard’s edge on the thirteenth was brought under the roof as a teaching, told again on an unearned day or joined to anything else. Each morning the surgeon took the body in the old order — the crust gone into old horn two inches off with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, the thread stiff and unwiped because nobody has ever been told to wipe it, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. He kept 435, 436 and 437 exact, six months and two hundred and fifty-five through two hundred and fifty-seven days told by nobody, and filed six honest answers 445 through 450 on the sixth place, two to each day, each exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, not one a doctrine. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of all three days, grain turned under wool and unfigured, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand, charcoal unread, widow’s mark untouched because a tending day is not an opening and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word in a term already ended with the loan uncalled; with Jorra the bent finger led at the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise ungiven against the burned slate at five. Ilva’s fear advanced and stayed unpaid: on Silt 12 a second neighbour at the well asked whether a count kept in wood would be taken at the next reading, and her hand went flat over the fold before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both; he filed the asking beside the offer and its return and the fifth shaping, with a finger between every pair, not a second offer, custom, tenth hand, witness, sale or calling of the loan, expressly unjoined to the clerk’s figure, the reported second slate and the near-reaching. On Silt 13 a man from Slate Row whose name was on no roll stood at the yard’s edge with loose hands and a patient face, asked nothing and saying nothing; he filed the face on its own tray beside the older record-first hands, no tenth hand, reader, witness, sale, payment or payer, not laid across the clerk’s figure, the reported second slate or the fourth reading and not brought under the roof as a lesson. In the small hours the hand came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing, let it go and came down flat on answer 450 as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking; there was no next hand in the room and he did not wipe the thread or lift the crust. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession; forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 127 (bonds).} Through Silt 8, 9 and 10 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the reported second slate of Silt 6 nor the hair-thin thaw of Silt 7 was made a teaching under the roof on a later day. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone past leather into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding and not a placing, the thread stiff in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a written line, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept 432, 433 and 434 exact, six months and two hundred and fifty-two through two hundred and fifty-four days told by nobody, stood none of them up as a threshold, doctrine or figure and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer and no key came under any roof. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, intake/hold/letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, her finger on the shelf’s top so the charcoal stayed unread, lips on a two-gapped row, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool unfigured, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, widow’s mark untouched, the fold righted without a look at his face or a second fold — and on Silt 10 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr Clay’s fourth reading and the bell, giving the wicker no instruction and no reason, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing. He watched the order of Berr’s reaching as a surgeon watches a hand leave a field before the dressing goes on — thumb wiped twice before touching nothing, finger over the figure through the sleeve, the speaker taken out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I} — and filed the order on a tray of its own with a finger between it and the face of the man from Slate Row and another between it and Hessa’s eighth, no tenth standing up in the empty place and no doctrine of the twice-wiped thumb. Four readings of the year stood behind one unsigned figure, four being four and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid, and he laid none of them across the neighbour’s near-reaching, the reported second slate or the hair-thin thaw, for an account that answers a reaching wants the hand that reached standing under it and none stood. With Tarn the sixth piece stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word with the loan uncalled in an ended term and the ear exposure rather than safety; with Jorra the dusty forearms were parted from clean as clot from vessel and the full note withheld from a master who would sing a pot before its time, the bent finger taking the cold out of the damper ahead of an unfinished sentence, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. In the small hours of Silt 10 the hand outside the wool came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took its small intake, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing, let it go and came straight down flat on the fold on answer 444 as a man puts away a tool where no next hand will find it; there was no next hand in the room, and he did not wipe the thread or lift the crust. No new scar, possession or change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 126 (bonds).} Through Silt 5, 6 and 7 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the reported second slate nor the hair-thin thaw was brought under the roof on the day after it was found. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone past leather into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding and not a placing, the thread stiff in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept 429, 430 and 431 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-nine through two hundred and fifty-one days told by nobody, stood none of them up as a threshold, doctrine or figure and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the three readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer and no key came under any roof. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket; coals told it was the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; the small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; her finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row; one glance at the cold clay jar with the hand shut half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire; dressed grain turned under wool unfigured; the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; the widow’s mark untouched, because a tending day is not an opening and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule. On Silt 7 she told the fire it was the thaw and did not tell the basket and asked nothing about the word at the well of the day before. With Tarn six pieces stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the knife at the edge of its sill, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach; \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} was found where put on all three days and not made a habit, and the ear-sentence stopped at the word that would call the loan, his valuable ear exposure and not safety in a term already ended. With Jorra meal-fine grey slate dust came past the bent finger and white in a fist-crease, dusty forearms parted from clean as clot from vessel, the wheel and a pot spoken to before any person, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld from any High Kiln master who would call it early, the bent finger taking the cold out of the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise to the men who burn slates neither given nor withdrawn. The offered figure went toward the well, looked at the light and went back into its sleeve, arriving nowhere; a woman sent for a pot’s cost got a note and not a price; the figure read over the covered grain did not know what it cost and the ink-neat space between figure and price carried no signature. Ilva’s strip stayed in her sleeve with her ninth hand nine, Hessa’s slate stayed unread up the road with her eighth hand eighth, Berr’s box stayed locked with the key gone up in a coat pocket, the clerk’s entered figure stayed a report from the landing, and the two market sightings stayed on separate trays with no eighth of either. The fire’s fifth was unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken 429, 430 and 431 days, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one; six hearings stood beside and never among with the seventh empty and the Drawing’s knock outside, nine record-first hands and nine stoppings with no tenth, and the file was exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. No new scar, wound, rank, power or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 125 (bonds).} Through Silt 2, 3 and 4 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the neighbour’s near-reaching at the shelf was not brought under the roof on the morning after as a teaching, a custom or a rule. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone past leather into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, not a placing, the thread stiff in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept 426, 427 and 428 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-six through two hundred and forty-eight days told by nobody, stood none of them up as a threshold, doctrine or figure, and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the three readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer and no key came under any roof. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, the small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, her finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stayed unread, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand shut half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool and unfigured, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, widow’s mark untouched, seven walked-around places once and not twice, fold righted without a second fold. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T097 with T060/T086, brushing T100 and T015/T041/T047):} in the afternoon of Silt 3 a neighbour with a pot reached past the bare board before her eyes found the basket, traced the top of the shelf where the charcoal lay beneath without going beneath it and without reading it, then let her finger go, without her seeing it, toward the empty place at his ear and stop a finger’s width short of the fold. She called the row’s old gap a thing the month’s turn brought in and the empty place a child’s appetite in one breath, made two rooms one absence without seeing it and went off with her pot. He took the reaching apart by the order of its parts — hand to board, eye to basket, mouth after both, the half-beat standing where a joining would have stood — and filed it on a place of its own beside the earlier shapings and the far-off finger, a further shaping, advanced and not paid, no joining, name, figure, third gap, fourth likeness, account or payer, not made his own and not laid across the twelve arithmetics, the three readings, the printed figure, the fifth shaping, the offered figure or the clerk’s entered figure. On Silt 4 it was not repeated and was not made a custom. With Tarn and Jorra the two quiet men kept their places at kindling and wheel-shed with their sentences and promises found where put and unjoined; Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken the same three numbers as the fire’s unpaid fifth. In the small hours the towel came out at the head of the bed as instruments do when a case is done; the hand outside the wool came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing, let it go as the note ended and came straight down flat on the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. There was no next hand in the room; he did not wipe the thread and did not lift the crust. Six honest answers, 427 through 432, stand on the sixth place and not one is a doctrine; no sixth hearing, tenth hand, tenth stopping, eighth opening, sixth shaping, eleventh arithmetic, signature, payer, witness, reader, third crust, name for a gap or ending came. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 124 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 29, 30 and Silt 1 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the third reading nor the two market sightings were brought under the roof as a teaching. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone past leather into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, not a placing, the thread frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept 423, 424 and 425 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-three through two hundred and forty-five days told by nobody, stood none of them up as a threshold, doctrine or figure, and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the three readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, intake/hold/letting-go with neither gap figured, finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand shut half over nothing, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, fold righted without a second fold, widow’s mark untouched — and on Ilmen 30 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade and stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell, carrying him home saying nothing. With Tarn six stood in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip, the knife at the edge of its sill, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put and not made a habit, the loan uncalled in an ended term and his valuable ear exposure and not safety; with Jorra the wheel-shed kept its silence, grey dust past the bent finger, the wheel and a pot spoken to before any person, the full note withheld from a High Kiln master and the bent finger out of the cold damper without a second holding of Ash 26, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. At the Cross on Ilmen 30 three readings of the year stood behind one unsigned figure — three being three and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid — and at the market’s edge a woman’s quarter-turned cup and a foundling’s stopped half-beat were filed on separate trays, a colour and a shape, never Fenna or Ulda, no eighth, no loaf, slate, sale, word or joining. Six honest answers, 421 through 426, stood on the sixth place, two to each day, and not one was a doctrine. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 123 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 26, 27 and 28 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the offer made at the well was not brought under the roof as a teaching, repeated on an unearned day or made a custom. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, the thread stiff in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept four hundred and twenty, twenty-one and twenty-two exact, six months and two hundred and forty through two hundred and forty-two days told by nobody, and stood none of them up as a threshold, doctrine or figure, and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the two readings of the year across one another, for paper is not a payer. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with a broken pot’s back, intake/hold/letting-go with neither gap figured, finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the cold clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with its half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, the fold righted without a second fold — and repair stayed apart from restoration and the widow’s mark hung where it hung, none of these days being an opening. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the small knife at the edge of its sill, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put on all three days and not made a habit; the ear-sentence stayed stopped at the calling word with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled in an ended term. With Jorra the wheel-shed silence held, dusty forearms parted from clean as clot from vessel, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld, the bent finger taken from the cold damper without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. \textbf{With Ilva the one change of the chapter, advanced and not paid (T080 with T090/T102):} at the yard well on Ilmen 26 a woman waiting her turn offered a figure for the month’s firings and put it toward the strip in Ilva’s sleeve; Ilva drew with the pail against her knee, clay pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam she does not scrub out, her hand flat over the fold before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, the half-beat in the gap. She answered the question put and not the one behind it — \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} — and the figure went from the fist toward the wood, looked at the light and went back into the sleeve, arriving nowhere, while the stick kept its notch and learned no name and nobody turned twice. The boy took the parts apart by their places — fist, eye, mouth, the half-beat — and filed the \textbf{offer and its return} on a place of its own beside her ninth record-first hand and the fifth shaping, with a finger between every pair, giving it no seller, buyer, reader, witness, account, tenth hand, payer or name and joining it to none of the well-asking, the clerk’s entered figure, the second man’s turned slate or the face at the yard’s edge. It is a reaching gathering interest toward the far-off hand that will one day lay the district’s private keepings together, and is not that hand; her fear is advanced and left unpaid, no figure was offered twice and she was not made a reader. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 420, 421 and 422 days and the fire’s fifth unpaid the same numbers. No bond was changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 122 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 23, 24 and 25 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the asking that came up at the well was not brought under the roof as a teaching and was not told a second time on a day that had earned only its twenty-fourth or its twenty-fifth. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, the thread stiff in the dry heat and unwiped because nobody has ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept four hundred and seventeen, eighteen and nineteen exact — six months and two hundred and thirty-seven through two hundred and thirty-nine days told by nobody — against a house that keeps its days badly in loaves pushed a finger’s width along a board and stopped, and stood none of the three numbers up as a threshold, doctrine or figure; six honest answers, 409 through 414, stand on the sixth place, two to each day, and not one is a doctrine. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with a broken pot’s back, intake/hold/letting-go with neither gap figured, finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, the fold righted without a second fold, the widow’s mark untouched — and on Ilmen 25 she added \emph{The fire doesn’t know you’re sorry. Feed it} to the fire and to no basket. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the knife at the edge of its sill, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put and not made a habit, the loan uncalled at the very end of an ended term. With Jorra meal-fine grey dust, dusty forearms parted as clot from vessel, the wheel spoken to before any person and the bent finger taken from the cold damper without the extra holding of Ash 26, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. With Ilva at the well on the twenty-third, her hand went to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, the strip unread and the ninth hand nine; she was expressly not the speaker of the asking and was not made a reader by its nearness. With Garl his name stayed unspoken and the fire’s fifth unpaid 417, 418 and 419 days, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one. Ilmen 30 (Day 424) stood five mornings beyond the close as a date and nothing of it was brought. No new scar, possession, power or rank.

\textbf{Ch 121 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 20, 21 and 22 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the second reading nor the second man’s passing was brought under the roof as a teaching. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — the crust leathery and hardened through the dry nights into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put and still a finding, the thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept four hundred and fourteen, fifteen and sixteen exact — six months and two hundred and thirty-four through two hundred and thirty-six days told by nobody — against a house that keeps its days badly in loaves pushed a finger’s width along a board and stopped, and did not stand the number up as a threshold, doctrine or figure. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of all three days — fire before basket, coals told the thaw, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing between staple and wire and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, the nineteen steps at the half-pace, the seven walked-around places once and not twice, the fold righted without a second fold, the widow’s mark untouched — and on Ilmen 20 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade and stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell. With Tarn the six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, the sentence found where put and not made a habit, the loan uncalled at the very end of an ended term. With Jorra the wheel-shed’s silence held, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld, the bent finger in the cold damper and out without a second holding of Ash 26, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. Hessa carried unread and her eighth stayed eight; Ilva drew at the well on Ilmen 21 with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine, expressly not the speaker of any word; Berr went up the road believing he had done a kindness and his low saying stayed on a place of its own; Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken and the fire’s fifth unpaid the same three numbers. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T080/T090, new T102):} on Ilmen 21 before first grey the second man’s direction down the bridge road and his narrow slate turned to the sleeve were filed on their own places beside the first man’s face, the clerk’s entered figure and the fifth shaping with a finger between every pair, and \textbf{two readings of the year now stand behind one unsigned figure} — two and not one account, the first not a thirteenth, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature and no doctrine out of two, twelve old arithmetics not laid across the two new ones. Answers 403 through 408 came out exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, six honest answers on the sixth place and not one a doctrine. No new scar, possession, rank or power and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 120 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 17, 18 and 19 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither Tarn’s withheld sentence nor the air less cold was brought under the roof as a teaching. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — the crust leathery and gone past the point where a child would still eat it, hardening into old horn through another dry night, the fold found where put and still a finding, the thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and cannot ask for; the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. He kept four hundred and eleven, twelve and thirteen exact — six months and two hundred and thirty-one through two hundred and thirty-three days told by nobody — against a house that keeps its days badly in loaves pushed a finger’s width along a board and stopped, and did not stand the number up as a threshold, doctrine or figure or lay the twelve old findings across the first of the new count, for paper is not a payer and no key came under any roof. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of all three days — fire before basket, coals told the thaw, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, the nineteen steps at the half-pace, the seven walked-around places once and not twice, the fold righted without a second fold, the widow’s mark untouched — and on the nineteenth she told the fire it was the thaw and said nothing of the air that had turned. \textbf{The chapter’s two changes, both advanced and NOT paid:} on Ilmen 18 at the kindling Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, passed a hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, and said no word to the wood — the sentence said on the seventeenth and said again on the nineteenth so the silence would be found where put and not a habit — and the boy filed the silence on a place of its own, a hand withdrawn from a field before the dressing goes on, not a tenth stopping, payment, hearing or rule; on Ilmen 19 air less cold came off the river and the river’s skin softened at one edge where the low note ran nearer under it, called weather by the yard and the thaw by Sella to the fire, and the boy filed the softening on a place of its own beside the clean dark line and the called-gone grey, not a sign, fourth covering, sixth shaping or payment, with no hand or payer under it and not made again. The clerk’s entered figure, Tarn’s degree and the face at the yard’s edge stayed on three places with a finger between every pair; the fifth shaping stayed on its own tray; Hessa’s eighth and Ilva’s ninth stayed eight and nine with no tenth. Six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 397 through 402, and not one is a doctrine. No present-tense break or tagged memory; no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 119 (bonds).} Through Ilmen 14, 15 and 16 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the clerk’s entered figure was not brought under the roof as a teaching. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — the crust gone leathery in the dry cold two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the empty place beside it holding the fold found where put and still a finding, not a placing, the thread stiff in the dry heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a face composed by cold is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be rewarmed slowly from the outside, never hurried, never rubbed, and that pink returning is the surface still lying over a cold core; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning. He kept four hundred and eight, nine and ten exact — six months and two hundred and twenty-eight through two hundred and thirty days told by nobody — against a house that keeps its days badly in loaves, glances and an unnamed space at the row’s end, and did not stand the number up as a threshold, a doctrine or a figure; the first arithmetic gone up the road was not laid across the twelve old findings to make a row come out even, for paper is not a payer, and no key to the box came under any roof. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of all three days — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing, the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, fold righted without a second fold — and she said nothing of the word that came up at the well. With Tarn at the kindling six pieces stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, knife at the edge of its sill, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, no turn of the head toward the landing, the degree not repeated as a habit or a rule, the loan uncalled at the very end of a term already ended and the Seed 16 breath unspent. With Jorra the dusty forearms were parted from clean as clot from vessel, the wheel and a pot spoken to before any person, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld from any High Kiln master who would call it early, and his bent finger put into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and out without the extra holding of Ash 26. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T090/T080):} on Ilmen 15 word came up the yard, from mouth to mouth with no body under it, that the soft-cuffed clerk still set below the north bridge at the out-of-line landing had entered a figure on his inward slate before he looked up to find the man who gave it — hand to the slate, eye to the person after, mouth after both, the half-beat in the gap. Nobody saw the hand or the slate, no man stood under the figure, no room was entered, no name spoken, no figure brought under any roof and no slate opened within reach of the basket: a report and not a sighting. He took it apart as a surgeon takes a field and filed the order on a place of its own with a finger between it and Tarn’s degree toward the landing and another between it and the face at the yard’s edge; it is the next reaching toward the loan that can hear and is \textbf{not} the calling of that loan, not a tenth hand, not a rule, not a sighting, not a witness, not a reader and not a payment. Ilva was offstage, her strip unread in her sleeve and her ninth hand nine, expressly not the speaker; Hessa was not a sighting and her eighth hand stayed eighth. On Ilmen 14 the man from Slate Row stood again at the yard’s edge with his hands loose, his face filed among the older record-first hands and not counted. No present-tense break and no tagged memory; no new scar, possession, power or rank and no change of voice.
