Six answers are filed on the sixth place, the ninety-first down at once on the river’s note, the ninety-second held for the small intake, the ninety-third held through the bell’s absent stroke and supplied with no stroke, the ninety-fourth carried across the silence in the room that does not touch, the ninety-fifth kept to the river’s own interval, and the ninety-sixth holding one rhythm for the small intake and a second, laid apart, across the little silence after a count that had ended in the other room. The file turned out on the towel is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, the charcoal stays unread, the ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five askings with no witness, the seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given, and Smoke 30 and the first firing of Frost stand ahead and unbrought (T071/T072, T088, T061/T082, T015/T041/T047, T077, T058/T079, T100, T080, T101, T036/T076, T006).

Through Smoke 22–24 he is two hundred and sixty-one, then sixty-two, then sixty-three days old, six months and eighty-one through eighty-three days, told by nobody. The third working week gathers toward Smoke’s last reading and settles nothing: no Account-day, market, Cross or bell, and Smoke 30 six mornings ahead and unbrought. In the plain work of the mornings he registers that the house keeps itself by \textbf{not-doings} --- two lines unswept, the mark untouched, the charcoal unread, the fifth pull unsupplied, the loan uncalled, no number spoken over the basket, the crust not lifted --- and keeps the seeing as a finding with no payer, not a grievance, a lesson or a doctrine. He does not lay the house’s omissions across his own kept empty intervals, for a joining would want a payer and none stands; the absence of the joining is itself kept. Six answers are filed on the sixth place, the ninety-seventh held for the small intake, the ninety-eighth through one whole interval of the river, the ninety-ninth down before the letting-go of a borrowed count, the hundredth carried across the little silence after a count in the room that does not touch, the hundred and first down on the river’s note and not on the kiln’s gap, and the hundred and second kept with the little silence after the house’s count left empty on its own place and not crossed. The file turned out on the towel is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the three counts stay in three places, the widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, the ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five askings with no witness, the seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given, and Smoke 30 and the first firing of Frost stand ahead and unbrought (T071/T072, T088, T061/T082, T077, T080, T101, T058/T079, T100, T083/T085, T064, T036/T076, T006, T009/T013/T092, T098, T060/T086).

Through Smoke 25–27, Days 264–266, three more lived days under the Vail roof, the boy comes into his two hundred and sixty-sixth day with nobody telling him what the number would count and one hundred and eight honest answers standing on the sixth place. The third working week gathers toward Smoke’s last reading and settles nothing. The chapter’s finding is that a thing can be handled as closely as a hand can examine it and still enter nothing — Sella turns the dressed grain piece by piece for damp and rot on Smoke 26 — and the finding is kept on a place of its own, not a lesson, grievance or doctrine, not laid across the house’s not-doings or his own kept gaps, with a finger between and no payer named. Its physical counterpart is the hand on the hundred and eighth answer going on past the river’s next note to the one after it, holding two intervals with the silence between kept empty and no second house count borrowed, which he makes nothing of and will not let stand up as a gift. The ownerless row question gathers one further shaping, a report of an asking and not a sixth asking, with no witness and no row named; the ninth hand stays nine with Ilva’s strip unread. Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given; Jorra’s promise stays ungiven and \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed; Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and sixty-six days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the count crosses into Smoke 28 unspent.

Through Frost 1–3, Days 270–272, three more lived days under the Vail roof, the boy comes into his two hundred and seventy-second day with nobody telling him what the number would count and one hundred and twenty honest answers standing on the sixth place. Frost comes on in its own light and goes out without a boundary drawn, and the month’s first firing on Frost 2 gives the chapter its one meaningful change: Sella goes to the kiln mouth before any word, holds the widow’s mark one breath, lifts the clay lid with the back of a hand and tips the coal under a broken pot, and the fire takes with its fifth still missing and its payer unnamed, nobody praising it or naming what it mended. He keeps the not-making as a finding with no payer, does not make four openings into a rule, and does not lay the household’s refusal across his own kept gaps, for a joining would want a payer and none stands; the rule of the mark is held exactly, with the touch at no other hour. On the last answer the hand sets a held interval beside an empty interval with a finger between and makes neither agree with the missing fifth, and the six answerings of these three days are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The grain stays covered and unfigured, the third arithmetic unread in Berr’s box; Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has not given, Jorra’s promise stays ungiven, Ilva’s ninth hand stays nine, the row question stays at five with no witness, and Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-two days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, and the count crosses into Frost 4 unspent.

Through Frost 4–6, Days 273–275, the working week begins by degrees and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and seventy-three days old and goes out of it two hundred and seventy-five — six months and ninety-three to six months and ninety-five days, nobody saying either figure. The count reaches two hundred and seventy-five exact with one hundred and twenty-six honest answers on the sixth place, and the six answers of these three days — a borrowed intake held, a letting-go left outside, one house rhythm carried across the little silence, two intakes held apart with a finger between, a separation made by ending early, and the held interval laid beside the empty interval — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The chapter’s one change is Sella’s: on Frost 5 her finger goes beneath the loaf shelf and stays two counted breaths where it once stayed one, and comes away unread. He files it and forbids it to stand up as a cause, a payment, a gift or a rule. The first firing of Frost stays behind the household with no lesson or payer, four openings remain four, the grain stays covered and unfigured, the seven places go around with a look and no number, and nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 7–9, Days 276–278, the working week goes out as it came in and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and seventy-six days old and goes out of it two hundred and seventy-eight — six months and ninety-six to six months and ninety-eight days, nobody saying either figure. The count reaches two hundred and seventy-eight exact with one hundred and thirty-two honest answers on the sixth place, and the six answers of these three days — one house rhythm carried across the river’s interval with no fifth borrowed, an ending made early with the letting-go left whole, two intakes held apart with a finger between, a bridge laid between a counted breath’s intake and the next hold over the river’s note, a held interval set beside an empty interval, and the river’s own small intake set beside a counted hold — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The chapter’s one meaningful change is the stayed frost: on Frost 8 the white the frost wrote on the well lip does not go when the sun is up as it went on Frost 4, and stays past noon and the going of the light onto Frost 9; the rope stiffens, the trough takes a skin and the coals are banked an hour earlier, and on Frost 9 Sella lifts a plate of ice and sets it out of the path of feet. The yard calls all of it weather, no figure is given, and nothing is made of it — no sign, lesson, mending, cause or payer, and Frost 10 does not pay it. He keeps each movement on a place of its own with a finger between and makes no fourth likeness a cause; the dressed grain is turned twice for damp and stays covered and unfigured, the seven places go around with a look and no number, and nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 10–12, Days 279–281, the count goes from two hundred and seventy-eight to \textbf{two hundred and eighty-one exact}, six months and ninety-nine days to six months and one hundred and one days told by nobody, with one hundred and thirty-eight honest answers on the sixth place and the fire’s fifth unpaid the same three days with its payer unnamed. The chapter’s one meaningful change is public and cannot be undone: Frost’s first Account-day comes to the Cross, Berr Clay reads \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, calls the levy and denies it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and goes off with the box locked and the first true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness; the district’s arithmetic changes for the month while the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and the reading knows nothing of the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15 or the dressed grain covered under wool at the rack end. Nothing of the reading comes back under the Vail roof as lesson, sign, mending, figure or payment. The six answers of these three days — a house rhythm carried across a counted silence, the heard bell’s gap set beside a held breath, a letting-go left whole, two intakes bridged over the river’s note, an intake held through the silence after its letting-go, and the held interval set beside the empty interval with a finger between — are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. He keeps the stayed frost, the plate of ice, the covered grain and the house’s not-doings on places of their own apart from his own gaps, makes no fourth likeness a cause and no doctrine of four openings, and lets Frost 20 stand eight mornings ahead, unbrought. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 13–15, Days 282–284, the second working week is lived one dated day at a time and settles nothing. He comes into it two hundred and eighty-two days old and goes out of it two hundred and eighty-four — six months and one hundred and two days to six months and one hundred and four days, nobody saying either figure. Three counts stay in three places, the fire’s fifth unpaid through all three days with its payer unnamed, six hearings stay six with no seventh, and the body is inventoried in its old order and entered nowhere: one crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and wrist, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform. The chapter’s one meaningful change is a saying arrived nowhere on the afternoon of Frost 14: a woman at the yard well, speaking to the boards and not into the basket, said that the runner who carries Berr Clay’s slate once carried a figure that named a person she knew. He takes it apart as a surgeon takes a wound apart and files it on a place of its own beside Hessa Rale’s eighth record-first hand with a finger between — a shaping toward the far-off day she must choose whether to read what she has carried, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a tenth hand, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness and not paid. He does not make Hessa a reader and does not join the saying to Ilva’s strip a pace away, and one stray saying does not stand up as a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands. Six answers take the sixth place from one hundred and thirty-eight to one hundred and forty-four, the last setting the held interval beside the empty interval with a finger between and neither promoted; each is exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. The stayed frost, the plate of ice and the covered grain go forward unfigured, the row stays at five askings with no witness, Tarn’s seventh year stands at its very end and has not given, Jorra’s promise stays sealed, and Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-four days. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Bone 10–12, Days 309–311, three more lived days under the Vail roof with one morning at the Cross, the boy comes into his three hundred and eleventh day with nobody telling him what the number would count and one hundred and ninety-eight honest answers standing on the sixth place. The count goes from three hundred and eight to three hundred and eleven exact, six months and one hundred and twenty-nine through one hundred and thirty-one days told by nobody, and the carried fire’s fifth stays unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed. The chapter’s one meaningful change is public and cannot be undone: Bone’s first reading comes to the Cross and four arithmetics — three of Frost and Bone’s first — now stand behind one printed figure; the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space, four are four and not one account, and a rule made from them would want a payer put under all four where none stood. He keeps the finding on a place of its own with no payer under it, not a lesson, grievance, mending, doctrine or rule, and does not lay it across the house’s not-doings, the dressed grain covered and unfigured under wool, the four held changes on four places or his own kept gaps — the edges come near to touching and the finger goes between. A finding with no payer can be carried a long way without becoming a rule. Six answers, the hundred and ninety-third through the hundred and ninety-eighth, are exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the surgeon’s clean satisfaction at each exact coordination is checked by the infant’s louder want of the crust, and the checking is the work and not a virtue. The heard bell stays in its square beside the told, six hearings keep the seventh place empty, five openings in five months are five and not a rule, the burned slate stands at five, the row at five askings, nine hands and nine stoppings with no tenth, and Bone 20 stands five mornings ahead and unbrought. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Bone 22–24, Days 321–323, the boy comes into his three hundred and twenty-first morning and goes out of his three hundred and twenty-third with nobody telling him what either number counts — six months and one hundred and forty-one to one hundred and forty-three days, told by nobody — the count exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody at three hundred and twenty-three with two hundred and twenty-two honest answers standing on the sixth place. The chapter’s one meaningful change is not his: at the rack end on Bone 22 Sella lifts the wool from the dressed grain, takes a small handful and lets it fall back through her fingers onto the heap instead of spreading it, saying nothing and giving no figure, and never does it again on the twenty-third or twenty-fourth. He reads it as a surgeon lifts a dressing’s edge and lets it fall, and files it on a place of its own: not a fifth held change, sign, lesson, mending, cause, sixth arithmetic or rule, with a finger between it and the four held changes on four places and a finger between it and his own gaps, no payer standing, kept because it was true and not because it bought anything. The empty fingers of the next two mornings go beside it as a keeping and not as a second, for two would be a habit and a habit would want a payer. The surgeon’s clean satisfaction at a field left undisturbed is checked by the infant’s louder want of the crust two inches off, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the argument the work and not a virtue. Five arithmetics ride locked up the clay road under one unsigned figure — one in twelve printed and unchallenged, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature, five readings five and not one account — and the finding stays on a place of its own with no payer, not laid across the house’s not-doings, the covered grain, the four held changes, the handful, the two small objects of the hand or his own gaps; the edges nearly touch and the finger goes between. Ilva’s ninth hand at the well on Bone 23 and the strip unread in her sleeve is a second person keeping a figure where no slate can take it, filed beside the handful without joining them, for testing and keeping are two acts and neither pays for the other. The staying of Bone 15 and the early letting-go of Bone 17 stay two objects and are not made again; three counts stay in three places, six hearings keep the seventh empty, the heard bell stays beside the told, five openings stay five, the burned slate at five, the row at five askings, nine hands and nine stoppings with no tenth and the loan uncalled. Nothing is opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended, and Bone 30 stands six mornings ahead and unbrought.

\item Ch 128: Lived Days 435–436–437, Silt 11–12–13, Y.H. 814, Firstday to Thirdday, three days in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner on any of them, and the house took up its grammar as though nothing had turned. Four hundred and thirty-five, thirty-six and thirty-seven days old — six months and two hundred and fifty-five through two hundred and fifty-seven days — told by nobody, count 435 to 437 exact and the fire’s fifth unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken the same three numbers. Answers \textbf{445, 446} on Silt 11, \textbf{447, 448} on Silt 12, \textbf{449, 450} on Silt 13, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 445 through 450, and not one is a doctrine. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches off with its corner a hair off the wool, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. Sella kept the whole hearth grammar at both ends of all three days, the widow’s mark untouched because seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule, and carried him home at each going of the light saying nothing of the day. Tarn’s sentence was found where put in an ended term with the loan uncalled; Jorra’s bent finger led at the cold damper and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed. \textbf{The two advances, both advanced and NOT paid:} on Silt 12 a second neighbour at the well asked whether a count kept in wood would be taken at the next reading, and Ilva’s hand went flat over the fold before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, answering \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}; the boy filed the second asking on its own place beside the offer and its return and the fifth shaping (T080 with T090/T102), not a second offer, custom, tenth hand, witness, sale or calling of the loan, expressly unjoined to the clerk’s figure, the reported second slate and the near-reaching, and not repeated on Silt 13. On Silt 13 a man from Slate Row whose name was on no roll stood at the yard’s edge with loose hands and a patient face, nobody asking and he saying nothing; the boy filed the face on its own tray beside the older record-first hands, no tenth hand, reader, witness, sale, payment or payer, not laid across the clerk’s figure, the reported second slate or the fourth reading and not brought under the roof as a lesson (T090/T080 with T036/T076 and T035/T031). In the small hours of Silt 13 the hand came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing and came down flat on answer 450 as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking; there was no next hand, he did not wipe the thread or lift the crust, and four low pulls under the boards kept their silence where the fifth should have stood with nobody supplying the pull. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession; forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 127: Lived Days 432–433–434, Silt 8–10, Y.H. 814, Eighthday to Tenthday, three days in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; Silt 8 and 9 were ordinary tending days with no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner, and Silt 10 was the month’s first Account-day and market and the year’s fourth reading, earned by its own morning. Four hundred and thirty-two, thirty-three and thirty-four days old — six months and two hundred and fifty-two through two hundred and fifty-four days — told by nobody, count 432 to 434 exact and the fire’s fifth unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken the same three numbers, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one. Answers \textbf{439, 440} on Silt 8, \textbf{441, 442} on Silt 9, \textbf{443, 444} on Silt 10, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 439 through 444, and not one is a doctrine. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches off with its corner a hair off the wool, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint as at the end of a written line, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. Sella kept the whole hearth grammar at both ends of all three days, the widow’s mark untouched because seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule, and on Silt 10 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade and stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell. \textbf{The chapter’s one large change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047):} Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded square under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passed a finger over the figure through his sleeve, read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket once for the moot and once for the households that came late, called the levy, denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, sent a fist-number to a slate at the watch where it arrived nowhere, said something low to the block about kindness being entered with no anger and no triumph, and went off up the road with Silt’s fourth true subtraction locked in his box and the key gone up in a coat pocket that never comes back down, believing he had done a kindness. Four readings of the year now stand behind one unsigned figure, four being four and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature on the space and no doctrine out of four; twelve old arithmetics were not laid across the four to make a row come out even, for paper is not a payer. The boy filed Berr’s order of reaching on a tray of its own with a finger between it and the face of the man from Slate Row and another between it and Hessa’s eighth, no tenth standing up. Hessa went up the road before noon with the narrow slate edge-on and unread and was not made a reader by four figures; the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself; the market sold over the reading with figures left side by side on a turnip heap, a fist arriving nowhere and a note that was not a price; the green and the shape stayed sightings on separate trays. Tarn’s ear-sentence stopped at the calling word with the loan uncalled in an ended term; Jorra’s promise stayed ungiven against the burned slate at five; the reported second slate, the hair-thin thaw and the neighbour’s near-reaching stayed where put and were not joined to the reading. In the small hours of Silt 10 the hand outside the wool came up an inch toward the river’s note, took its small intake, held the interval on the note’s finishing, let it go and came straight down flat on the fold on answer 444 as a man puts away a tool where no next hand will find it; there was no next hand in the room, the thread unwiped and the crust unlifted, four low pulls under the boards with the fifth not supplied. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar, possession or change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 126: Lived Days 429–430–431, Silt 5–7, Y.H. 814, Fifthday to Seventhday, three ordinary tending days in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner on any of them and Silt 10 (Day 434) stands three mornings beyond the close, unbrought. Four hundred and twenty-nine, thirty and thirty-one days old — six months and two hundred and forty-nine through two hundred and fifty-one days — told by nobody, count 429 to 431 exact and the fire’s fifth unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken the same three numbers, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one. Answers \textbf{433, 434} on Silt 5, \textbf{435, 436} on Silt 6, \textbf{437, 438} on Silt 7, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 433 through 438, and not one is a doctrine. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. \textbf{The first advance, advanced and NOT paid (T080 with T090/T102):} in the afternoon of Silt 6 a word went around the yard well from mouth to mouth among the bucket-round with nobody standing under it that the woman who carries Berr Clay’s slate had taken up a second, narrower one held edge-on under her arm with the writing turned the same way toward her sleeve; no figure came off either slate and no name was spoken over either, her hand going to the slates before her eye to the yard and her mouth after both, the half-beat standing in the gap. He took the report apart by the place of each part and filed the second slate on a place of its own beside the eighth record-first hand, the offered figure and its return, the clerk’s entered figure brought up the yard as a report and the three likenesses of Slate Row, with a finger between every pair — not a reader made, not a ninth or tenth hand, not a witness, sale, sixth shaping, custom, payment, cause, rule or calling of the loan, and not laid across the twelve arithmetics, the three readings, the printed figure, the fifth shaping, the neighbour’s near-reaching or the two sightings. The runner’s reaching came nearer to a joining than it had ever come and was refused in the same breath; the woman was never on stage, was given no name, sheet, interior, errand or witness’s standing, and the word was not told again on Silt 7. \textbf{The second advance, advanced and NOT paid (T083/T085/T092 with T009/T013/T092):} in the afternoon of Silt 7 the grey called the thaw at the Vail corner lay a hair less distinct along one stretch where no broom had gone in two years, thickened in the dry cold with the faint sour tang of Ash, and the air off the river was less cold at one edge where the low note of water over water ran nearer under the winter skin, the tang thinner there; he found both where put, did not look twice, called them weather and made no sign, fourth covering, fourth likeness, sixth shaping, custom, payment or payer of either. Sella told the fire it was the thaw and did not tell the basket, and the two greys at the corner kept a finger between them, a thing left in place not a thing forgiven. With Sella the whole hearth grammar held at both ends of all three days, the widow’s mark untouched; with Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, his sentence found where put; with Jorra the dusty forearms, the wheel spoken to before any person and the bent finger at the damper stayed as they were, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise ungiven. In the small hours the hand came up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, held the interval whole on the note’s own finishing, let it go as the note ended and came straight down flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. There was no next hand in the room; he did not wipe the thread and did not lift the crust, four low pulls breathed under the floor and the fifth was not supplied. No present-tense break, no `**` tag, no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession and no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 125: Lived Days 426–427–428, Silt 2–4, Y.H. 814, Secondday to Fourthday, three ordinary tending days in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`, nothing skipped, poured into another or summarised; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner on any of them, and Silt 10 (Day 434) stands six mornings beyond the close, unbrought. Four hundred and twenty-six, twenty-seven and twenty-eight days old — six months and two hundred and forty-six through two hundred and forty-eight days — told by nobody, count 426 to 428 exact and the fire’s fifth unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken the same three numbers, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one. Answers \textbf{427, 428} on Silt 2, \textbf{429, 430} on Silt 3, \textbf{431, 432} on Silt 4, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 427 through 432, and not one is a doctrine. Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — crust gone past leather into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T097 with T060/T086, brushing T100 and T015/T041/T047):} on Silt 3 afternoon the neighbour with a pot reached past the bare board before her eyes found the basket, traced the shelf’s top where the charcoal lay beneath without going beneath or reading it, then let her finger go toward the empty place at his ear, stopping a finger’s width short of the fold; she named the old gap a thing the month’s turn brought in and the empty place a child’s appetite in one breath, made two rooms one absence without seeing it and went off with her pot. He took the reaching apart by fist, eye, mouth and the half-beat in the gap and filed it on a place of its own beside the earlier shapings and the far-off finger — a further shaping, advanced and not paid, no joining, name, figure, third gap, fourth likeness, account or payer, not made his own, not laid across the twelve arithmetics, the three readings, the printed figure, the fifth shaping, the offered figure or the clerk’s entered figure, and not repeated on Silt 4. Sella’s whole grammar held at both ends of all three days; the softening at the river’s skin was called weather and not looked twice; Tarn’s six and seventh were found where put and his ear-sentence stopped at the calling word; Jorra’s bent finger took the cold out of the damper and came out without a second holding of Ash 26, the promise neither given nor withdrawn; the two quiet men stayed unjoined; Garl’s name was unspoken the same three numbers as the fire’s fifth. Three readings of the year stood behind one unsigned figure, three being three and not one account. In the small hours the towel came out as instruments do when a case is done; the hand went up an inch toward the river’s note (the inch not a reach), took a small intake, held the interval whole on the note’s finishing, let it go and came down flat on the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. There was no next hand in the room; he did not wipe the thread and did not lift the crust; four low pulls breathed under the floor and the fifth was not supplied. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession, no payment, witness, reader or ending. Forward, not closed.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 124: Through Ilmen 29, 30 and Silt 1 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer and neither the third reading nor the two market sightings became a teaching. Each morning the surgeon took the body in the old order — crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear, fold found where put and still a finding, thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and wrist, the Afterdrop waiting — and the infant’s three wants quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. He kept 423, 424 and 425 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-three through two hundred and forty-five days told by nobody, answers \textbf{421–426} two to each day on the sixth place, not one a doctrine, and did not lay the twelve old arithmetics or the three readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer. On Ilmen 30 three readings of the year stood behind one unsigned figure, three being three and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid, no signature; at the market a woman’s quarter-turned cup with clay in her nail crescents and a pale cord-mark and a foundling’s head stopped a half-beat after a note were filed on separate trays — a colour and a shape, never Fenna or Ulda, no eighth, no loaf, slate, sale, word, name or joining, no crossing under the roof. In the small hours the hand went up an inch toward the river’s note, held the interval whole on the note’s own finishing under the winter skin, let it go as the note ended and came down flat on the fold as a man puts away a tool there is no next hand to find. He did not wipe the thread or lift the crust. Sella’s whole grammar held at both ends of all three days, the pot rim two inches beyond reach, the mark untouched at every hour that was not an opening; on Ilmen 30 she set the basket in the moot-post’s shade and stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell. Tarn’s six and seventh, his sentence found where put and the loan uncalled, and Jorra’s dust, wheel, withheld note and bent finger at the damper held as they stood. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no sixth hearing, tenth hand, eighth opening, signature, payer or reader; no new scar, wound, rank, power or possession, no change of voice.

Each morning the surgeon took the body in its old order — the crust stiff and brown-edged, gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, past the point where a child would still eat it; the fold found where put and still a finding, not a placing; the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped because nobody has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopping at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it; the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — knowing a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and could not ask for; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T080 with T090/T102):} at the yard well on Ilmen 26 a woman waiting her turn shifted a pot from one hip to the other, brought a number up out of a shut fist, held it toward the light and put the fist toward the strip in Ilva’s sleeve, saying she could put a figure to the month’s firings. Ilva drew with the pail against her knee, the rope stiff in the dry cold giving its small rasp, clay dried pale in her nail crescents and finer rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb she did not scrub out; people noticed the pail first and the sleeve not at all. Her hand went flat over the fold before her eyes went to the asker and her mouth opened after both, the half-beat lying in the gap where a lesser observer would put an intention. She answered the question put and not the one behind it — \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} — and put the flat of her hand once more on the sleeve. The woman held the figure out a breath longer, shut her fist upon it and put it back into her sleeve, where it arrived nowhere; \emph{Then it’s a stick}, she said, and went back to the round, and nobody turned twice. No slate was opened within reach of the basket, no figure came off the wood, no reader was made and no name spoken over the notches. He took the order apart by the place of each part — fist, eye, mouth, the half-beat in the gap — and gave the fist no figure and the sleeve no motive, for a motive is a payer wearing a coat, and filed the \textbf{offer and its return} on a place of its own beside her ninth record-first hand and the fifth shaping, with a finger between every pair: not a sale, reader, tenth hand, payer, account or sixth shaping, not the calling of the loan and not joined to the well-asking, the clerk’s entered figure, the second man’s turned slate or the face at the yard’s edge, but a reaching gathering interest toward the far-off hand that will one day lay the district’s private keepings together and not that hand. Her fear is advanced and unpaid. Offstage on the twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth she was not made a reader and no figure was offered twice. Costs came as directions and went away as weather: the fist opened toward the well and shut again, a woman sent for a pot’s cost got a note and not a price, and the arithmetic read over grain covered at home did not know what it cost and had no signature between figure and price. Sella’s whole grammar held at both ends of every day; Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip with \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put; Jorra parted dusty from clean as clot from vessel and took his bent finger out of the cold damper without the extra holding of Ash 26. The called-gone grey stayed beside the left-in-place ridge, the softening at the river’s skin was called weather and seven openings in seven months were seven and not a rule. In the small hours the towel came out as instruments do when a case is done; six hearings stood with the seventh empty and the Drawing’s knock outside, nine hands and nine stoppings with no tenth, the three counts staying three and the two readings two and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid. The hand came up an inch toward the note, held the interval whole on its own finishing, let it go as the note ended and came straight down flat against the fold on answer 420. He did not wipe the thread or lift the crust. Four low pulls breathed under the floor and the fifth was not supplied. No present-tense break, no `**` tag, no new wound, growth, rank, power, scar or possession and no change of voice; forward, not closed.

\item Ch 107: Lived Days 372–373–374, Stone 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, carried under the Vail kiln-house roof, down into the Clay Yard on the afternoons, to the yard well on the thirteenth, to the clay road’s edge on the fourteenth and to the kindling and wheel-shed on the afternoons, three hundred and seventy-two, seventy-three and seventy-four days old — six months and one hundred and ninety-two, ninety-three and ninety-four days — told by nobody, the count going 371 to 374 exact with \textbf{three hundred and twenty-four honest answers} standing on the sixth place (319 in the small hours of the thirteenth, 320 at its close, 321 in the small hours of the fourteenth, 322 at its close, 323 in the morning of the fifteenth and 324 in the small hours at the very end), each a small intake taken from the room whose floor does not touch his, held whole on the river’s note’s own finishing under the winter skin, let go as the note ended and the hand straight down and laid flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking — exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer. Each morning the surgeon’s register took the body in the old order — the leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool and its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof had ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and he knew the order in which a body gives heat up is the reverse of the order in which it takes it back and that pink returning to a face is surface still cold and not the core, and could do nothing with the knowledge; the infant’s want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. Sella came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and no handful, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, glanced once at the clay jar with her hand half over nothing, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and left the widow’s mark untouched because a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a yard, a road, a going of the light and a bed are not openings and no eighth opening was made due. The yard went around its seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out; the gone white frost, the skinned trough and the silt-clouded plate of ice stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair, and the river’s winter skin was found where put beside water over water and not spent. On the thirteenth Ilva drew at the well with the rope stiff and the clay pale in her nail crescents, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, answering \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} with the notched birch strip unread and no figure off the wood; the boy filed her order of reaching as the \textbf{ninth} record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa Rale’s eighth and filed no tenth, and she was expressly not the speaker of any voice. On the fourteenth Hessa came \textbf{down} the clay road out of Greybank with Berr’s narrow slate edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned toward her sleeve, the second strap let out and dried road-mud unbrushed on the shortened skirt; her hand went to the slate before her eyes to the yard and nothing pressed where the writing was, she gave no figure, read nothing aloud and did not look into the basket, and the boy filed the turning of the writing toward herself beside the Ash 6 sighting with a finger between, no reader, no witness, no fifth shaping of the Frost 14 well-saying and no payment, her eighth hand staying eight with no tenth. Jorra kept the wheel-shed edge, parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel with meal-fine grey slate dust white in a fist-crease, gave no name to the men who went low into the back room before first grey, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the full note known three turns ahead, and let his bent finger lead into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence — one iron with two bites — taking it out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, T097 with T060/T086 advanced and NOT paid:} at the going of the light on the fifteenth Sella set him on his bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and tucked the wool into the empty place beside the crust — a small keeping with no word, no third crust, no name spoken over the place, no look toward his face and no instruction to the basket, her hand resting the half-beat longer than the setting needed and the thread left frozen and unwiped. He took the interval apart by what was there and by what was not and filed it on a place of its own beside the crust’s gap, the shelf’s two gaps, the gone pan’s round ring and the field’s empty place: expressly not a joining of rooms, not a third crust, not a gift, not a payment, no payer, not a sixth held object, not a seventh or eighth, not a habit, a way, a sign, a hearing, a mending, a cause or a rule, gathered once and not made again, found where put, gathering interest toward the far-off finger that will one day lay shelf and fold together and call the joining an account — and that hand is not his and has not come. The surgeon read the movement as a hand at the edge of a wound that closes nothing, exact and worth nothing at two inches of air; the infant wanted the crust lifted and the thread wiped; both true, the second louder, neither winning. \item Ch 106: Lived Days 369–370–371, Stone 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, carried under the Vail roof, down into the Clay Yard on all three afternoons, to the Cross on Stone 10 and to the Hearth Drawing two doors down on Stone 12, set at the edge of the light where he could see and not join; three hundred and sixty-nine, seventy and seventy-one days old — six months and one hundred and eighty-nine, ninety and ninety-one days — told by nobody, the count going 368 to 371 exact and \textbf{three hundred and eighteen honest answers} standing on the sixth place (313 in the moot-post’s shade; 314 in the small hours at the roof; 315 at the yard well’s morning; 316 at the close of Stone 11; 317 after the carry home from the Drawing; 318 in the small hours at the very end), each a small intake held whole on the river’s note’s own finishing under the ice, let go as the note ended and the hand straight down and laid flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking — exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across none of the held objects. Stone 10 was the month’s first Account-day and market and the tenth arithmetic of the year: Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red cord folded, the sweet green of glaze at one mouth-corner and the smell of nothing at all, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, passed a finger over the figure through his sleeve, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket — once for the moot, once for the late households — called the levy, denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, said something low to the block about kindness being entered and went off with the box locked and Stone’s first true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; \textbf{ten readings stand behind one unsigned figure and ten are ten and not one account}, the figure read still not the figure paid and no doctrine out of ten. Hessa took the slate up the road before noon with the writing to her sleeve and answered the question put; the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for an uncalled measure; the silent green-mouthed woman turned a cup a quarter and the small shape in cast-offs caught the green sliver and went dull, a seventh of each with no eighth; the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept in its square beside the told. Each morning the surgeon’s register took the body in its old order — stiff brown-edged barley crust two inches off with its hair-lifted corner, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped, nobody under any roof ever given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform — and the composed face was not composure, a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and rewarming must be slow and from the outside, never rubbed, never set too near the fire; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. On Stone 11 Ilva drew at the well with the pail against her knee and answered what Stone’s firings had taken with \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, the notched birch strip unread and filed as the \textbf{ninth} record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa’s eighth and no tenth; she was expressly not the speaker of any voice. \textbf{The chapter’s earned event, Stone 12’s Hearth Drawing, was rendered only from the basket at the edge of the light:} a cuff soft from washing and folded back twice, a flat leather satchel, a cold iron tube out of a roll of wool, fingertips grey the colour of skimmed milk gone off, a hand to the slate before the eyes to the bed, and the collector’s ordinary untroubled hand filed on a tray of its own and joined to none; the neighbour on the board-bed gave under the tube with a small flat knock and was left with a pale round place, not a wound and no blood, and the boy did \textbf{not} make the knock a seventh hearing, for a hearing wants a source standing and the room was seen from a basket, not entered. A rekindled child three days out of a thin return went worse on the third day — grey fingertips, red at the hairline, a pink face that was surface still cold and not the core — and the room called it a graft settling; the mother held a cup of warm milk she never drank, and the death-house women corrected the boy without knowing he had spoken. He knew the order in which a body takes heat back and the order in which it gives it up, and could not speak, reach, warm or say \emph{leave it} or \emph{warm it slowly}. He set the room beside the birth room, the Vail kiln-house and the Court’s room with a finger between every pair, wrote no cause across any of them and joined none to the burned slate, the Greybank saying or the Ash directions. Sella carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of where they had been, set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen. Tarn kept six in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, found the Ash 14 breath and Bone 26 thumb’s resting where put and not made again, brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, Seed 16 breath unspent and loan uncalled; Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel before any person, withheld the full note three turns ahead and put his bent finger into the cold damper with its two bites without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise under the wheel-shed neither given nor withdrawn. The widow’s mark was untouched on all three days, a market, a well, a yard and a Drawing not being openings and no eighth made due; the river’s winter skin was found where put and not spent on the reading or the Drawing; the fire’s fifth stayed unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken 369, 370 and 371 days. No new wound, scar, rank, power or possession; no seventh hearing, tenth hand, tenth stopping, eighth opening or payer supplied; no lesson, cause, payment or ending. Forward, not closed.

Ilva came once to the well on Ash 22 with her strip unread, her hand to sleeve before eyes to asker and mouth after both, the ninth hand nine with no tenth and expressly not the speaker of any voice; she was offstage on the twenty-third and twenty-fourth. The direction of the twenty-third did not repeat and nothing from any of the three days bought a lesson under this roof. No rank, power, scar or possession; forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 99: Lived Days 348–349–350, Ash 19–21, Ninthday to Firstday, carried under the Vail roof, down into the Clay Yard and to the Cross on Ash 20; three hundred and forty-eight, forty-nine and fifty days old — six months and one hundred and sixty-eight, sixty-nine and seventy days — told by nobody. No collector up or down the clay road and no runner on any road; Ash 20 was the dark month’s second Account-day and market, earned by its own morning, with no market, Cross or bell on Ash 19 or 21, and Ash 30 (Day 359) stood nine mornings ahead and was named only as a date. Nothing from Ash 19, 20 or 21 crossed forward as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Each morning the surgeon’s register took the body in its old order: the stiff brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone leathery in the dry kiln heat, its corner a hair off the wool, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform. He knew the composed face is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from outside and slowly, never rubbed and never set too near the fire, and the infant’s want of the crust lifted two inches, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle was louder than the surgeon’s knowing, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the argument the work. Three counts in three places — the carried fire’s four low pulls with its fifth unpaid and its payer unnamed 348, 349 and 350 days, the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot, and the river’s water over water through the finger’s-width door, never numbered among the hearings — did not become one; six hearings stood beside and never among with the seventh place empty, the sixth the small flat knock out of a woman as the men lifted her; the heard bell stayed in its square beside the told with nobody crossing himself; the charcoal stayed unread beneath Sella’s finger and the dressed grain lay turned under wool and unfigured with no handful lifted. Six answers were filed, \textbf{271} through \textbf{276}, one per scene, each a small intake taken from the room whose floor does not touch his, the interval held whole on the river’s note’s own finishing, the hand straight down and laid back against the fold as a tool put away where the next hand will find it — the note had done before the hand came down, so no letting-go was early again and the hand did not stay. \textbf{Two hundred and seventy-six honest answers} stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047, held with T077):} on Ash 20 Ash’s second true subtraction went up the clay road locked and unread in Berr’s box beside the three of Frost and the first, second and third of Bone; \textbf{eight arithmetics of the year now stand behind one printed figure, eight are eight and not one account}, the printed figure still one in twelve and unchallenged, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space between. He filed the finding on a place of its own with no payer and did not lay it across the house’s not-doings, the covered grain and the empty fingers, the five held objects, the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath, the handful, the thumb’s resting, the two small objects of the hand, the sixth opening, the Ash 5 joining, the Ash 17 direction, the fourth shaping, the turned writing, the strip in the sleeve or his own kept gaps; the edges came near to touching and the finger went between. Nothing in the reading answered the hand that went in on Seed 15, the man carried out on Day 188, the dressed grain under wool, the carried fire’s missing fifth, the word that went up the terrace or the room shut with the damper closed, and no doctrine stood up out of eight, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. Berr called the levy and denied it with \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never I, taking himself out of his own sentence, said something low to the block about kindness being entered and went off believing he had done a kindness; there was no anger and no triumph in it. At the close he lay on his bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf under the roof, awake, silent, cold, carried and untouched in every particular, one stiff crust two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, the file open on the towel with every gap left gap. No wound, growth in capacity, rank, power, scar or possession; no answer became a reach, hearing, stopping, gift, habit or rule; the count closes at \textbf{350 exact}, six months and one hundred and seventy days told by nobody. Body inventoried in the surgeon’s old order each morning: the stiff brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone leathery in the dry kiln heat, its corner a hair off the wool, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. The fire took, answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and thirty-one days; \textbf{six openings in six months — Tallow 1, Ember 1, Smoke 1, Frost 2, Bone 2 and Ash 2 — are six and not a rule}, no seventh made due, nobody praising it, naming what it mended, entering a slate or making a lesson, sign, mending, cause or payer of it, the five behind not looked at again as signs or payments, and the mark not touched again at shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, dusk or going of the light. He took the opening by the small sounds — the scrape of the clay lid, the coal under the broken pot, the fire taking in fours with the gap — and filed it on a sixth place of its own with a finger’s width around it, noting only that the fifth pull was still missing and joining it to none. Sella kept the hearth grammar on all three mornings and at each going of the light: fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs to pot and fire and the crack showing, dressed grain turned under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, the grey streak at her temple pale and coal-black hair pushed back with the burn-wrist. Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the knife at the very edge of its sill, the ear-sentence brought to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent, his chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring holding light, his stroke over the bright patch without the half-check, the warm loft stone cold in its unmarked pot, the thumb’s resting of Bone 26 checked and not made again on any of the three days, and \emph{Yes, house} to an early and a late thaw with the late kept because it puts off the paying. On Ash 2 Ilva drew at the well with the rope stiff in the Ash cold, clay pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam, and to a woman asking what the firings of Ash had taken answered \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve and the notched strip unread; the boy filed the order of reaching as the ninth record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa Rale’s eighth, filed no tenth, made no figure of the open slate a pace away and joined her keeping to none (T080 advanced, not paid). Nothing on Ash 3 was opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended. Forward, not closed.

Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red cord of his office folded under his coat and the sweet green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay the smell of nothing at all; he wiped his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened with the writing inward, passed a finger over the figure, read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the late households — called the levy and denied it with \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, taking himself out of his own sentence, and went off up the road with the box locked and Bone’s third true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. Six arithmetics of the year now stand behind one printed figure; six are six and not one account, the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space and a rule made from six is refused for want of a payer. Sella set the basket in the moot-post’s thin shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through the reading and the bell; Hessa took the slate up the road toward Greybank unread, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the landing, the green and the shape stayed sightings with no eighth, the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told. Ilva answered once at the well on Bone 29 with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine; on Bone 28 and 30 she was offstage. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken three hundred and twenty-seven, twenty-eight and twenty-nine days and his tile debt uncalled. No collector came up or went down the clay road; nothing opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended, and the keeping of the number the only honest work there was to do.

The boy read a hand laid on a place a man had decided not to open and left there unopened, and filed it on a place of its own with a finger between it and the nine stoppings, the four held changes, the handful let fall at the rack end on Bone 22 and his own gaps — not a tenth stopping, not the seventh year given, not a payment, not a fifth held change, not a hearing, not a near-full answer, not a mending and not a rule, no payer standing and not made again on Bone 27, when Tarn said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late and kept the late because it puts off the paying. Sella kept the whole hearth grammar on all three mornings, went to the fire before the basket, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot and said \emph{The house will keep it}, kept the charcoal unread and the two gaps unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar with her hand half over nothing, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs and the crack showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and lifted no handful, set the rim two inches beyond his reach with a half-beat and no look toward his face, righted the fold without a look and left the thread, touched the widow’s mark at no hour, carried him at the half-pace from every open slate around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, and on Bone 27 set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, her hand resting the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away. The chapter’s one meaningful change was not his: at the going of the light on Bone 8, while Jorra’s bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, Tarn’s broom checked half a beat behind it on the flagstones and went on toward the road without a word or a turn of the head, the Seed 22 half-check and the Day 171 flagstone movement returned changed after a hundred and thirty-six days; neither man named the other’s silence and the loan that can hear was not called. He filed it on the flagstone’s own place beside the Day 161 fraction, the Day 166 shelf beat and the Frost 5 returned beat: four held changes on four places, and he forbade them to stand up and call themselves a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stood. It was not made again on the seventh or ninth. Six hearings stayed six beside and never among with the seventh place empty, nine stoppings stayed nine with no tenth, nine hands stayed nine with Ilva’s strip unread, the burned slate stayed at five with a finger between, the row at five askings with no witness, three shapings of the well-saying with no fourth, and the stayed frost, skinned trough and clouded plate weather entered nowhere. Bone 10 (Day 309), the month’s first Account-day and market, stood one morning ahead and was not brought into a day that had not earned it. No bond changed hands, no power gained, no new scar or possession.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 84: Days 303, 304 and 305, Bone 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday, carried under the Vail roof and in the Clay Yard on all three days, three hundred and three, four and five days old — six months and one hundred and twenty-three, twenty-four and twenty-five days — nobody saying any figure. Body inventoried each day in the old order: the leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its unnamed empty place and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop beyond a warming nobody here will perform; a cold patient cannot clot, will seem better before he is worse and must be warmed slowly from the outside, and the wanting of the crust two inches off is louder than the knowing, the checking being the work and not a virtue. The count closed at \textbf{305 exact} and the hand filed six answers, the \textbf{one hundred and eighty-first} through the \textbf{one hundred and eighty-sixth}: the small intake let go whole on the river’s note; an empty interval beside a held interval with the finger between; the half-beat of the pot’s set-down beside a small intake; the empty interval between the ownerless voice and the weather’s answer kept empty; a small intake let go whole as a restraint and not a payment; and the final intake let go whole on the river’s low note. Sella turned the dressed grain beneath the wool with progressively lighter touches and no figure, set the pot rim two inches beyond his reach with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and lifted the twice-mended pot with her thumb first where the wire crossed the crack. Ilva answered once at the well on Bone 6 with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine; the stayed frost, skinned trough and clouded plate stayed weather entered nowhere; Berr’s three arithmetics stayed locked up the road; Tarn kept six and the held seventh with the loan uncalled; Jorra kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and his promise ungiven; Garl stayed a coat, a hollow seat, a crack left showing and an uncalled tile debt with his name unspoken three hundred and five days. No powers used, no rank change, no experiment, no new scar or possession, no bond changed hands, nothing opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended, and no payer stood to any of it.

\item Ch 78: Lived Days 285–287, Frost 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, three dated days in six scenes, two hundred and eighty-five through two hundred and eighty-seven days old — six months and one hundred and five days to six months and one hundred and seven days — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). On Frost 17 Ilva was glimpsed once at the well with her hand toward her sleeve, answering \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}; he filed no tenth hand and did not join her strip to the Frost 14 well-saying, which stayed one saying with a finger between it and Hessa Rale’s eighth hand, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness and not paid, and never making Hessa a reader (T080). The stayed frost on the well lip, the skinned trough and the plate of ice clouded with silt on its flat stone were called weather and entered nowhere; the dressed grain lay covered and unfigured under wool, read over on the tenth by a number that did not know its cost; Frost’s first arithmetic stayed locked in Berr’s box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid (T083/T085 held, T077, T015/T041/T047). At the close the file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap and every tray parted by a finger’s width, the hand laid back against the fold on the hundred and fiftieth answer, the crust still two inches off and its empty place unnamed, and the river’s low note going quiet after the hand came down. No power was used, no rank gained, nothing opened, named, called, paid or ended.

He added that a figure may be carried in a slate by someone who will not read it, that a voice can arrive nowhere with no owner to be asked, that a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands, and that a letting-go kept whole is not a freedom or a gift, because a freedom wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything.
