No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 75: Days 276–278, Frost 7–9, Seventhday to Ninthday. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the crease at the left shoulder on its peg behind the door, the hollow wheel-seat that Sella will let nobody fill, the clean dark line at the Vail corner with the finer grey called the thaw beside it, unswept both, the proverb gone to a pot and the fire and never to a person, and the debt against a firing of tiles circling without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-eight days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 7, 8 or 9 (T009/T013/T092). Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven (T036/T076). The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-six through two hundred and seventy-eight days (T088); Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the widow’s mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months (T058/T079). On Frost 9 she lifted a plate of ice from the trough with the back of the broken pot and set it out of the path of feet, and the yard called the stayed frost and the ice weather with no figure and no payer (T083/T085 advanced, not paid). The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own gaps stay on separate places for want of a payer, and joined neither to this absence or to any other (T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 74: Days 273–275, Frost 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat that Sella will let nobody fill, the proverb gone to a pot and the fire and never to a person, and the debt against a firing of tiles circling without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-five days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 4, 5 or 6 (T009/T013/T092). Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven (T036/T076). The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-three through two hundred and seventy-five days (T088); Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the widow’s mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months (T058/T079). The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own gaps stay on separate places for want of a payer, and joined neither to this absence or to any other (T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; his name, the stone warmed at his hearth and the house’s silence around him are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: Present throughout Days 2 and 3 as the shape of the house. The kiln’s breath he kept alive was counted in fours and a gap; his seat stayed hollow, his coat stayed on its peg, his Ash ridge grew, and his proverb \emph{leave the crack showing} was said in the house’s voice to the pot and the fire. The house’s private roll was spoken around: he was entered on it, and the foundling’s name would be entered there in a careful hand. The charred edge of a slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. No collector was called.

\item Ch 3: Day 4, Account-day. Present as what is left where it lay. The kiln took one breath behind the boy as he was carried out and missed the next; the lead on Berr’s breath and the red cord folded square came with the confirmation of Sella’s widow’s mark, and the debt Garl left against the tiles went spoken around, neither called nor settled. In the afternoon a barrow of grey Ash went out through the north gate toward the Bone Orchard, the same work that went out every market-day; the boy put it with the ridge under the Vail skirting board and the charred slate in the kiln ash, and nobody explained any of the three.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The banked coals held under their ash through the night and the kiln breathed four, four and a gap; the hollow seat stayed unfilled, the salt-stiff coat stayed on its peg, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept. The charred edge of the slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and nobody said them to the boy. The debt against the tiles lay uncalled while the year’s first measure was called and entered in another house, and the boy kept the two facts side by side.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. The coals held under ash through the night and the kiln took its breath in fours and a gap; the salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept and not to be swept before the Last Day. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles stayed uncalled while a number of days to Kindling went around the house as a closed fist.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Days 10--14. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. His coat kept its salt-stiff shape on the peg, his wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years on the left, the charred slate lay in the kiln ash unexamined, and his sayings went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The kiln took its breath in fours and missed one on all five days. On Stone 19 Sella measured the ridge with her thumb, near two thumbs here and a finger more two doors down, and Tarn offered to check it; she said leave it, it’ll be swept on the Last Day. On Stone 20, Account-day, the debt against the firing of tiles was spoken around at the Cross and never named, a space in Berr’s sentence shaped like the hollow seat, and Berr went around it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Days 15--24. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all ten days: the kiln breathing four, four and a gap; the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, the Ash ridge running to the corner and turning it without a break and not to be swept before the Last Day, the charred slate lying in the kiln ash unexamined. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself}, \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. On Stone 29 Sella laid her thumb in the Vail ridge and then in the death-house ridge, a finger thicker, and came back without saying which was which; the uncalled debt against the tiles went around the door talk in a careful circle with no word for the thing circled, and a woman at the tubs said the grey would be left until the Last Day, burned next morning and called dealt with. On Stone 30 Berr went around the debt at the Cross without naming it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Days 25--30. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all six days: the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, and the proverb going to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. His name was not spoken under the Vail roof on the Remembering and Sella went around it as around Ash in a corner. The ridge turned its corner without a break, was measured by one thumb at Vail and a finger’s width thicker two doors down on the Last Day, and was left where it lay through the baking; on Ilmen 1 it was burned in the morning and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the corner was a clean dark line. The uncalled debt against the tiles stayed uncalled through the turn of the year and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Days 31–37. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The place where the Ash ridge had turned its corner for a year and two days was a clean dark line, burned on Ilmen 1 and called dealt with by a neighbour with a pail of water while Sella stood over it with a broom and said nothing; it was not swept. His salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door and the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years and nobody filled it. The proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket --- leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled --- and went on being said after the grey line along the wall was gone. The debt against the firing of tiles lay where it lay through another turning of the year, neither paid nor settled nor done with, and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Days 38–44. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Ilmen 9, the day Dessa Silt was lifted out of the brook and no collector came, his salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash, and the proverb went to the fire and the pot and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. On Ilmen 11 Sella measured the clean dark line where his Ash ridge had turned with one thumb and the ridge two doors down with the same thumb, a finger’s width wider, and left both where they lay. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four, and the debt against the firing of tiles stayed neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Day 45 a brine-gull took a coal not yet cold out of the carried fire he first kept, and one warmth less went out of the world with no slate the poorer; the boy kept the subtraction. The salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg, the wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the ridge had turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still being said after the crack was gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled nor done with while no collector came for the woman the brook took nine mornings ago.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On all seven days the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket; the carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled, the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was entered in no slate and missed in no account, and another woman lay sixteen mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Days 55--60. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: salt-stiff coat on its peg, the hollow seat nobody fills, the charred slate in the kiln ash, the clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept (T009, T013, T031). His proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, said over a pot with no crack and a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and broken pot at four, four and a gap; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was fifteen days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account (T088, T065). On Ilmen 29 Sella laid one thumb in his clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetched no broom; a barrow of grey went out toward the Bone Orchard at the last market (T013). On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathered beside the clean dark line and was called thaw and not swept (T092). The debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled (T009); another woman lay twenty-two mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. A new, finer hairline of grey gathered beside it on Silt 2 and lay there all week, unswept and called thaw; the boy set the two lines in two places. His proverb went to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-two days gone; the debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled while another woman lay twenty-nine mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 15: Days 68–74, Silt 9–15. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing through the flood and the going of it: salt-stiff coat on its peg, hollow seat nobody fills, charred slate in the kiln ash and clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The Ilm came up over the Fishstairs and stood a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it went off into mud neither had been swept; the boy set the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey in three places that did not touch. His proverb went to a pot with no crack over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone; the debt against the tiles lay where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lay thirty-six mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 70: Days 261–263, Smoke 22–24. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-three days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 22, 23 or 24. Tarn kept Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence came to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-three days; the boy kept the house’s not-doings --- the uncalled loan among them --- as a finding with no payer, held apart from his own kept gaps with a finger between and joined to no absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 71: Days 264–266, Smoke 25–27. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-six days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 25, 26 or 27. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-four, sixty-five and sixty-six days. The boy kept the finding that a thing handled closely still enters nothing on a place of its own, and kept the house’s not-doings apart from his own gaps with a finger between, joining neither to this absence or to any other absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 72: Days 267–269, Smoke 28–30, Eighthday to Tenthday. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-nine days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 28, 29 or 30. Tarn kept Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-four, sixty-five and sixty-six days gone on to two hundred and sixty-seven, sixty-eight and sixty-nine. Smoke’s third arithmetic went up the road in Berr’s locked box on the 30th and changed nothing under this roof; the boy kept the finding that three readings are three and not one account on a place of its own and did not lay it across this absence or any other (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082, T015/T041/T047). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 73: Days 270–272, Frost 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-two days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 1, 2 or 3. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days, stopping there as a remembered \textbf{ninth} stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy through two hundred and seventy-two days; Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the widow’s mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the house’s not-doings and his own gaps stay on separate places for want of a payer, and joined neither to this absence or to any other (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082, T058/T079). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}
}

Sixteen and built like a gate hinge: tall for a clay boy, narrow, with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and a permanent bend in his left little finger from a splinter off the wheel when he was eleven. He cuts his hair short so Ash cannot nest in it, which is a thing the district notices and he never explains. His eyes do not finish sentences; they go to the door, to the fire, to the wheel, and come back without reporting. He smells of damp clay, tallow and the sweetish edge of lead glaze carried up from High Kiln on a bad wind. The thing people notice first is his hands, which are the hands of a thrower and have been working since he was nine. The thing they notice last is that he never looks at Sella when she speaks to him, though he obeys her instantly.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
Short, flat, declarative. He asks almost no questions, and when he does it is the tool rather than the clay: \emph{Is it dry? Did you fire it? Who wrote it?} He speaks to the wheel and to the pots as other men speak to animals, and only then to people. When he is angry he gets quieter, the way Sella does, and the household has learned to read the lowering of his voice as a weather signal. He never says \emph{with} or \emph{against} when \emph{I haven’t said} will do.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “The wheel doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.”

\item “You want me to say it. I’m not saying it.”

\item “Sella. Don’t feed him from your own dish. He’s not Vail.”

\item “A slate burns in four minutes. Four. I’ve timed it.”

\item “I didn’t say I was with them. I said I wasn’t against them. That’s different. In this district it isn’t, but it’s what I said.”

\item “He’s not Vail.” --- said in the kiln-house at first light, refused an answer, and sealed by the boy’s arrival.

\item “You’ll do.” --- to the pot on the wheel, in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either.

\item “It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.” --- to the wheel before anyone, said again on Day 140 of a pot he told \emph{You’ll do} while keeping its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time.

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
He is the son of Garl and Sella Vail, and he took the wheel at thirteen when Garl died in the Long Cold and did not come back and nobody came to draw him. The wheel had been Garl’s for twenty years and the seat was worn hollow; Jorra has spent three years trying to fill that hollow with his own weight. He has thrown pots since he was nine, fired them since eleven, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves his hands, though he will not say so in front of the kiln-masters, who would call it early and make something of it. His house has remembered the Ash Rising since Y.H. 668, when children were taken and the rising was put down by a man with a list; the memory is kept not in stories but in the way certain doors are never closed and certain names are never entered. Since he was fourteen men from the Broken Slates have come into the back room of the kiln-house and spoken in low voices. He has listened to all of them and told none of them yes.

He watched Enna, his sister, die of the second chill at four, and has never forgiven the fire for being warm while she cooled. He watched his father die and was sent to find a collector and could not cross the ford, and has never asked whether he was sent too late or whether he was sent at all. When Corin arrived he said one sentence — \emph{He’s not Vail} — and has said nothing about it since, which in that house is a form of argument.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
A father who went uncollected, a sister who went cold in a warm room, and a wheel he was given before he was ready. He fears Sella will die with something unsaid and leave him holding the house and the lie together. He fears the Broken Slates will decide for him what he is, because he has not decided and the longer he waits the more their decision looks like his own. He fears the boy most of all, because the boy hears things. His contradiction: he is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and he is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill. He has never once thought these two facts cannot live in the same man.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wants the wheel to stay in the house and the fire to hold and nobody to write the boy down as Vail without asking him first. He thinks he wants Sella to say that he has done well with the wheel. What he needs is to learn that burning a slate does not return a person to you, and that the anger he has been nursing for three years is not his alone — it has been lent to him by men who intend to collect on it.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Ch 128 (bonds).} At the wheel-shed edge on Silt 11, 12 and 13 the household straightened around his silence without a word from anybody; nothing from the second asking at the well, the Slate Row face at the yard’s edge, the softening at the river’s skin, Tarn’s sentence found where put, the four readings behind one unsigned figure or the four ownerless directions came under the shed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. He came through the finger’s-width door with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past his bent little finger and white in a fist-crease, kept dusty forearms and clean on one tray and parted them as clot from vessel, gave no name to the men in the back room and no word that the room was cold, and the broken ones under the lowest rack stayed entered by nobody. He spoke to the wheel before any person — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knew its full note three turns ahead and withheld it from any High Kiln master who would call it early. On all three mornings his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, taking the cold out of the fingertip and coming out without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, one piece of iron holding and taking and no Grathic word covering both. With Corin nothing changed: the boy lay under the roof unwritten, \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise under the shed was neither given nor withdrawn while the burned slate stood at five, the shut-room tellings at two and the four ownerless directions apart and unspent; Tarn’s sentence found where put was filed by the boy beside his as two quiet men under one roof and not a custom. No new scar, wound, rank or possession, no change of voice, nothing called or paid.

\textbf{Ch 86 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands with Jorra through Bone 10–12. He kept the wheel and the household’s shape at the shed’s edge, parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person and withheld the note known three turns ahead from a High Kiln master who would call it early. His bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence; the men who went low into the back room before first grey got no name and no word that the room was cold. He grew quieter at the fifth burned-slate telling and the household straightened around the quiet without an order, the claim gathering interest against a promise he neither paid nor refused. Sella’s reading went up the road and back without changing anything under the wheel-shed, and Tarn’s stroke went over the bright patch without the half-check while Jorra’s finger stood where it stood. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name was neither given nor withdrawn. No name given, no debt paid, no bond paid, sold, named or spoken.

\textbf{Sella Vail} — his mother. He believes she took Corin in to replace Enna and to keep the house’s standing after Garl died. She has never contradicted him. Every obedience he gives her is therefore double: it is love and it is a correction neither of them will make. \emph{Ch 2:} she announced the taking and he answered \emph{he’s not Vail}; she got quieter and gave him no answer at all. He went on working, did not look at her, and shifted the damper before she had finished telling him to.

\textbf{Corin} — the foundling. Jorra was the first in the house to notice that the boy turns his head toward a pot before anyone taps it, and that he does it to hear the note, not the noise. He has told nobody. He resents the boy for being given a bed in the house while the clay-bound hand sleeps in the loft, and he cannot stop watching him. \emph{Ch 2:} the foundling arrived under the roof and nobody wrote him as Vail, which is what Jorra wanted and what he cannot bear. He spoke to the wheel, to the pots and once to Tarn about a rasp out of its place, and never addressed the boy.

\textbf{Alda Reed} — attended Enna’s death and Corin’s birth, and has never met Jorra’s eye for longer than a moment. He knows she wrote something down the night Enna died and has never asked to see it, because asking would make it a thing between them.

\textbf{Tarn} — the Vail’s clay-bound hand. Jorra treats him as a brother when the wheel needs him and as a servant when it does not. Tarn has decided to hate him for it and keeps failing, because Jorra once sat up all night with him through a fever and has never mentioned it. \emph{Ch 2:} Tarn was given the loft while the foundling was given the bed, and said so in one sentence to Sella. Jorra said nothing; he has never defended the household’s arithmetic and never contests it.

\textbf{Berr Clay, the Thane of Clay} — Jorra threw a stone at his door in Y.H. 810 and denied it. The Thane suspects the boy is with the Broken Slates and lets him be, which Jorra finds more frightening than being watched.

\textbf{Ch 4.} Sella’s hand went to the mark before the kiln and not at the bank; he shifted the damper before she had finished and again at dusk, and did not take up her silence about the back room. The boy was at the edge of his notice as a thing that hears: he spoke to the pots and not to him, and came in from the back room with slate dust worked into his forearms --- grey and fine, not slip --- and said \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody. He wanted the boy outside the name Vail and the hollow seat his, and did not say either.

\textbf{Ch 5.} The wheel took the house into its rhythm again with slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no slate dust on Stone 13 or Stone 15; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask which it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands were on it, and shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low. He did not say the back room was cold. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as it had been on the hour it was spoken, and the foundling went on being carried under the roof without a Vail name, which is what Jorra wanted and what he could not bear.

\textbf{Ch 6.} On all five days he came in from the shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger, and no slate dust; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask what it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and \emph{the shoulder’s thick}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and moved the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low, going in with the bent finger ahead of his hand. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the basket or the bed. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed; the foundling went on being carried under the roof unwritten.

\textbf{Ch 7.} On Stone 23, after five mornings of clean bone-coloured slip, he came in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger and said nothing about where he had been; the boy read the arranged face the way he had once read a resident who kept his eyes on a chart. He told the pot she would want a thinner slip, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and went to the damper before Sella had finished, the bent finger going in first. On Stone 25 the forearms were clean again and he kept dusty and clean as two entries; on Stone 29 the sweeping talk made him quieter and the yard straightened around it without an order. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so in front of a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it; the boy knows this about him as he knows the bent finger, and keeps both where questions can last for years. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed through the year’s last market.

\textbf{Ch 8.} Through the Five the wheel-shed gave him bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger leading at the damper; he moved the damper before Sella had finished and did not say the back room was cold. No slate dust came after the Last Day and he never mentioned the back room; he did not look toward the bed or the basket. On the Last Day the grey in the corners was still where it lay and the baking went on around it, and he went quieter as the sweeping talk went around. On Ilmen 1 he worked the slip toward the thaw and the pits with the same forearms and the same silence, and the foundling went into the new year carried under the roof without a Vail name.

\textbf{Ch 9.} On Ilmen 4 he came in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger and said nothing about where he had been; on the other mornings the forearms carried bone-coloured slip, and the boy kept the two states apart. He told a pot it would do, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, and went to the damper before Sella had finished, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand. He knew the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master. He agreed with nobody about the thaw and contradicted nobody, and his silence went around the yard as its own weather signal. He did not look toward the basket and did not say the back room was cold.

\textbf{Ch 10.} He comes in from the wheel-shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no grey slate dust worked into the creases past the bend of his little finger on the days the boy watches; on Ilmen 11 the bent finger goes in ahead of his hand at the damper and he moves it before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low, so she shuts her mouth on the instruction and gives it to the pot. He tells a pot \emph{You’ll do} and tells the wheel it does not care whose hands are on it, only if they are steady, and does not say the back room is cold. He does not look toward the basket or the bed, has not been told about the woman in the brook and has not asked. Garl’s proverb still goes to the pot and his own unfinished sentence still goes nowhere; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed through seven more days.

He told a pot \emph{You’ll do} and the wheel what it had been told a hundred times --- that it did not care whose hands were on it, only if they were steady --- and said nothing of the room off the shed, whose door kept its finger’s width of open. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed or the basket. Garl’s salt-stiff coat kept a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean, and the clean dark line where the ridge had turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as on the hour it was spoken.

\textbf{Ch 128 (Days 435–437, Silt 11–13).} The wheel-shed kept its silence through three tending days and the household straightened around it without a word from anybody. Meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and white in a fist-crease, dusty forearms parted from clean as clot from vessel, no name for the men in the back room and no word that the room was cold; the wheel and a pot spoken to before any person, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld from any High Kiln master who would call it early. On all three mornings his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, took the cold out of the fingertip, moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and came out without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time — one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word covering both mercies. The second asking at the well, the Slate Row face at the yard’s edge and the four readings behind one unsigned figure brought no meaning under the shed. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise to the men who burn slates neither given nor withdrawn against the burned slate at five and the four ownerless directions; Tarn’s sentence found where put was filed by the boy beside his as two quiet men under one roof and not a custom, and nothing from the yard was laid across either silence. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, nothing called or paid; forward, not closed.

He enters at the wheel with his weight in the hollow his father wore and has spent three years failing to fill --- slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms, the left little finger bent from a splinter at eleven, a story about a fight he tells because a fight sounds more like him. In Chapter 2 he says one flat sentence about the foundling and is refused an answer, and the sentence is sealed by the boy’s arrival: a child lies under the roof and nobody has written him as Vail. He does not look at his mother while obeying her instantly, speaks to the pots before people, goes quiet when the levy is spoken of, and has given none of the men who come into the back room a word they can carry away. He is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill, and has never once thought the two facts cannot live in the same man. Through the middle tend of Grain his dust, his wheel and his withheld note kept their old order while the burned-slate word held at four and the pot sayings at three; the wrong-wind voice on Grain 15 let one saying stand without a pot lost, and the promise of the boy’s name stayed ungiven (T035/T031/T065/T095 held, T061/T082).

Sella does not take it further. The boy watches the dust and wants to know which slate was broken, and whether it was a birth-slate, and keeps the questions where questions can last for years.

He keeps the two states of his forearms as one man’s two mornings and the boy keeps them on the same tray without asking which slate was broken or whether it was a birth-slate. Broken birth-slates stay buried under the lowest rack and the space above them is gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel and the pots and never to the basket or the bed, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master who would call it early and make something of it, and moves the damper with the bent finger leading ahead of Sella’s sentence so that the end of her instruction arrives at the pot. The yard straightens around his silence without an order. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name stays ungiven and not withdrawn, while the hollow seat waits for his weight and the foundling goes on being carried under the roof unwritten.

On Days 126 through 128 the wheel goes on and the back room stays shut. He is offstage on Reed 7, 8 and 9 except for the one morning of Day 127, and on that morning men unnamed come up the Clay Yard before first grey with their collars high and speak low in the room off the wheel-shed; the door stands a finger’s width open and is not entered, and he gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold. He comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bend of the little finger — not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel — keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates lie under the lowest rack and nobody enters them. It cares if they’re steady}, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do} and knows its full note before it leaves the wheel; when a kiln-master come up from High Kiln would call it early and make something of it he withholds the knowing and says nothing a slate could carry. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence, moves the tongue a hair’s breadth and leaves it standing, and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted; the boy reads the iron once more as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, and files it as an object worth nothing joined to no kiln. Tarn’s stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones keep the shallow bright patch where it stopped; neither man names the other’s silence, and when the ear’s sentence comes a second time to the threshold of the word that night he does not ask about it. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed, the promise of the foundling’s name to the slate-burners is neither given nor withdrawn, and the two tellings of the shut counting room stay beside the iron with no third. Nothing is named, opened, joined or paid.

The men in the room off the shed remain three or four shapes with no names, and the dust ground small as meal past the bent finger still waits for the question he will not ask. The damper holds mercy and mutilation in one bite with no Grathic word for both; the promise of the foundling’s name to the slate-burners is neither given nor withdrawn. The equality under the roof holds at its moved place, Tarn’s stroke going on without the half-check and neither man naming the other’s silence.

On Days 138 through 140 the household keeps the equality it moved to by fractions and the broken slates stay unentered. On Day 140, before first grey, three or four men with their collars high go low into the finger’s-width-open back room; he gives them no name and does not say the room was cold. He comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before anyone --- \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} --- tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds it from a High Kiln kiln-master who says the pot is singing before its time and will sing itself out early; the knowing goes on the tray of near-full answers, advanced and not paid. His bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, moves the tongue a hair’s breadth and leaves it standing, and the boy reads the iron once more as mercy and mutilation in one bite with no Grathic word for both, filed joined to no kiln. At the hearth he does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room; the loan that can hear stays uncalled and Tarn’s sixth stopping draws a breath that is not spent. The two tellings of the shut counting room stand beside the damper with no third, and the men in the back room are not joined to them. Nothing is said of the foundling’s name, no slate is burned in his hearing, and the promise stays where it was put.

Through Reed 22 and 23 he keeps the room and the wheel between himself and the boy. Through Bone 10–12, Days 309–311, he keeps the wheel and the household’s shape at the shed’s edge: meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and white in the creases of a fist that had opened, dusty forearms parted from clean as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, the wheel told it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady, a pot told \emph{You’ll do} and its full note known three turns ahead and withheld on the near-full tray beside the hearings. Three or more men go low into the back room before first grey on the mornings of all three days and get no name and no word that the room was cold; his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies. He grows quieter as the burned-slate word goes around, and the household straightens around the quiet without an order. The fifth telling stands at five with a finger between the fifth and the four, no witness standing, no hand named at the flame and no sixth due on a day that has not earned one, and the seed waits on the far-off calling-in of his promise — not a confession and not a payment. The shut-room tellings stay at two, the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart, and the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness. Bone’s first reading goes up the road in Berr’s box and changes nothing under the wheel-shed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise stays ungiven. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Bone 22–24, Days 321–323, he keeps the wheel-shed edge and the household straightens around his silence. Each day he came through the finger’s-width door with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; kept dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray parted as clot from vessel, asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, spoke to the wheel before anyone and told a pot \emph{You’ll do} with no welcome and no unkindness. He knew the full note a pot would give three turns ahead, with air under it and a want in it, and withheld it on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them from a High Kiln master who would have called it early. Three or more men went low into the back room before first grey and got no name from him and no word that the room was cold. His bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence on Bone 22 and 24 and the household straightened around the waiting; he read one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word for both mercies and no slate entered. He grew quieter as the burned-slate saying went around and the household straightened around the quiet without an order; the fifth telling stood at five with a finger between the fifth and the four, no witness standing and no sixth due on a day that had not earned one, and the claim went on gathering interest against his promise to the men who burn slates, the promise neither given nor withdrawn. The shut-room tellings stood at two, the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart, the row at five askings with no witness and the Frost 14 saying at three shapings beside Hessa Rale’s eighth hand. Sella’s handful at the rack end brought no word under the wheel-shed and was not joined to his dust, his damper or his promise; the finding that five readings are five and not one account stayed on a place of its own with no payer. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar, possession or change of voice.

Came through with the morning’s meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; parted dusty forearms from clean ones as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, kept them on one tray and asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates stayed under the lowest rack where the yard went around them and entered them into nothing (T009/T013/T092). Three or more men unnamed went low and quiet into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and got no name from him, and he did not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stayed two with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). Spoke to the wheel before he spoke to anyone (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome and no unkindness, knew its full note three turns before it left his hands with air under it and a want in it, and withheld the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them (T061/T082). The three shapings of the pot saying stayed sayings — sings itself out early, not heard from since, gone quiet on every row come the thaw — with no fourth likeness made a cause, no pot lost and no name given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188; the burned-slate word stood at four and the shut-room tellings at two with no fifth and no third (T035/T031/T065/T095 held, not paid). \textbf{The Grain 21 question gained a second asking} on the afternoon of Grain 23: a voice with no owner went over the boards, the weather answered and the price of barley after it, the voice went up the terrace and the row stood where it stood; he filed it on its own seventh place beside the first with a finger between the two and fingers between it and the sayings, the slate, the shut-room tellings, the six hearings and the count. Two askings are not one witness; he supplied no witness, named no row, made no cause and let it stand as a seed for the far-off day a witness stands somewhere and can be asked (T101 advanced, not paid). He grew quieter whenever the burned-slate word went around and the household straightened around the quiet without an order, the quiet going before him into the shed the way a cold air goes before a door. When Sella’s voice went low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger went into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence, took the cold out of the fingertip and gave nothing back, held until the sentence reached the pot, moved a hair’s breadth and was left standing — a remembered repetition and not a change made again, joined to no kiln and paired with no other fraction; the iron was one piece with two bites, with no word in Grathic for both mercies (T062). \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as a lid nobody had tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the foundling’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn; he did not look toward the bed or the basket. The dressed grain stayed covered under wool with no figure, the returning-line place was gone around with a look and no number, and Berr, Hessa and the clerk stayed offstage. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar, possession or change of voice.

\end{itemize}

Three or more men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and got no name from him, and he did not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stayed two with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). The burned-slate word had come a fourth time over the boards from Slate Row and arrived nowhere, a direction with no hand at the flame and no figure at its foot; he grew quieter whenever it went around and the household straightened around the quiet without an order, the quiet going before him into the shed the way a cold air goes before a door. No fifth telling came and no third telling of the shut room (T035/T031/T065/T095 held, not paid). A wrong-wind kiln-hand come up off High Kiln let one of the three shapings stand over the boards on Grain 21 — \emph{a pot gone quiet on every row come the thaw} — and went on to the weather and the price of barley; he let it stand as a saying and no more, taking it apart and setting it back, with no fourth likeness made a cause, no lesson, no name for what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 and no pot lost; the sweet edge of lead glaze came up on the wrong wind, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it, a direction and not a second edge paid (T064). When Sella’s voice went low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of her sentence and stood there, the iron taking the cold out of the fingertip and giving nothing back; he held until the sentence reached the pot, moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and left it standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate, one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies (T062). On Grain 20 he was offstage at the market. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar, possession or change of voice.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; the wheel, the hollow seat and his objecting are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: At first light stood at the wheel with slip-coloured forearms and the bent finger, told the pot the slip was too thick and it would crack at the shoulder, and went quiet when the levy was spoken of. When Sella said the boy would come under the roof he said \emph{he’s not Vail}, did not look at her, and was not answered. On the third day sat in the hollow seat as the boy was carried in, obeyed Sella’s instruction about the damper before she had finished, told a pot \emph{you’ll do}, spoke once to Tarn about a rasp, and never addressed the child. Nobody wrote the foundling as Vail.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. At the wheel with slip dried to old bone on both forearms and the bent little finger, speaking to the pots and not to the boy, obeying Sella before she had finished and shifting the damper before she had finished again. At dusk came in from the back room with slate dust worked into the forearms --- grey and fine, not slip --- and said \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody, answering no question about where he had been and giving Sella nothing to take further. Garl’s coat kept its salt shape on its peg and his hollow seat stayed unfilled; he did not look at the basket.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. At the wheel with slip dried to old bone up both forearms, the bent little finger and no slate dust on Stone 13 or Stone 15; told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and the wheel \emph{it doesn’t care whose hands}, and did not look toward the basket. Shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low and went quieter when the levy was spoken around. Did not say the back room was cold, did not take up Sella’s silence, and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed while the foundling went on being carried under the roof unwritten.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

Told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and \emph{the shoulder’s thick; I’ll thin it}, and told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady. Shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low and left the end of her sentence where it was, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand. Did not say the back room was cold, did not look toward the basket or the bed, and went quieter when the levy, the uncalled debt and the reading were spoken around. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as it had been on the hour it was spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Days 15--24. On Stone 21 came in from the wheel-shed with bone-coloured slip and no slate dust, said she would want a thinner slip and went to the damper before Sella had finished. On Stone 22 worked at the wheel turning a pot nobody would look at twice. On Stone 23, after five clean mornings, came in with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger, said nothing about where he had been, told the pot \emph{she’ll want a thinner slip} and the wheel \emph{it doesn’t care whose hands; it cares if they’re steady}, and took the damper ahead of Sella’s instruction; a pot set down on the bench gave nothing and he did not look toward the bed. On Stone 25 the forearms were clean of dust again and he said the shoulder was thick and he would thin it. On Stone 27 spoke to a pot and the damper and let the thaw argument go over him. On Stone 28 told a pot it would do and moved the damper ahead of Sella. On Stone 29 the sweeping talk made him quieter and the yard straightened; he moved the damper before she had finished, did not say the back room was cold, and did not look toward the bed, and the boy knew he could hear the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master. On Stone 30 he had moved the damper and not said the back room was cold. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed all ten days.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

No slate dust came after the Last Day, he did not say the back room was cold, did not look toward the bed or the basket, and went quieter as the Last Day sweeping talk went around; the grey lay in the corners through the baking. On Ilmen 1 worked the slip toward the thaw and the slip pits with the same forearms and the same silence. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed through the year’s turn and the boy went into 813 unwritten.

Three or more men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and got no name from him, and he did not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stayed two with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). Spoke to the wheel before he spoke to any person — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome and no unkindness, knew its full note three turns before it left his hands with air under it and a want in it, and withheld the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid (T061/T082). The three shapings of the pot saying stood as sayings with no fourth likeness made a cause; the burned-slate word held at four tellings out of Slate Row, still a direction arrived nowhere and still not a third telling of the shut room; the row question stood at five askings with no owner, witness, cause or row named and was not asked a sixth time (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). On Smoke 14 a pot set down wrong at the racks, out of a woman’s shadow and near the warm side of the wall, gave its high thin note before its time; the woman swept around it and said something practical about the slip, and he made no lesson of the sound, no fourth likeness a cause and no name for what ailed the man carried out on Day 188, and no pot was lost. A wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards and took it out again (T064). When Sella’s sentence went low his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of it, took the cold out of the fingertip, held until the end of it arrived at the pot, moved a hair’s breadth and was left standing — a remembered repetition paired with no other fraction, one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln (T062/T035). \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn. Smoke’s first reading stayed behind and unread under this roof and changed nothing here. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 68: Days 255, 256 and 257, Smoke 16–18, on stage at the wheel-shed edge, the cold damper, the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the Clay Yard on all three days. Came through each morning with the day’s meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip (T009/T013/T092); parted dusty forearms from clean ones as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, kept them on one tray and asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, while the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack were entered by nobody. Three or more men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and got no name from him, and he did not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stayed two with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). Spoke to the wheel before he spoke to any person — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome and no unkindness, knew its full note three turns before it left his hands with air under it and a want in it, and withheld the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid (T061/T082). Three shapings of the pot saying stood as sayings with no fourth likeness made a cause; the premature note from Smoke 14 stood beside them on its own place; the burned-slate word stood at four from Slate Row, a direction arrived nowhere and not a fifth telling; the row question stood at five askings with no owner, witness, cause or row named and was not asked a sixth (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). When Sella’s sentence went low and unfinished (\emph{The fire’s low. It wants---}) his bent finger went into the cold iron of the damper ahead of the end of it, took the cold out of the fingertip, held until the sentence arrived at the pot, moved a hair’s breadth and was left standing — one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln and paired with no other fraction (T062). He did not ask about the ear while Tarn did not ask about the room, and the two silences stayed unjoined. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as a lid nobody had tried to lift in three years, and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}
