On the nineteenth she told the fire it was the thaw and did not tell the basket, and said nothing of the softening at the river’s skin, which the yard called weather and nobody owned. With Tarn the sixth piece stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the sentence spoken on the seventeenth, withheld on the eighteenth and spoken again on the nineteenth, and the loan uncalled at the end of an ended term; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper and came out without the extra holding of Ash 26. No new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 119 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 14, 15 and 16 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and neither the word that came up at the well nor the figure the clerk entered before he looked up was brought under the roof as a teaching. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the tighter wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and wire and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration as a surgeon keeps a graft apart from a cure, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest at the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found where put and stayed a finding, not a placing (T097/T060/T086 advanced, not paid). \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a basket, a well and a going of the light are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth came due. With Tarn the sixth piece stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, the loan uncalled at the end of an ended term and the degree not repeated; with Jorra her unfinished sentence went to the pot through his bent finger standing in the cold damper and came out without the extra holding of Ash 26, and he gave no name to the men in the back room or to the man who came to the yard’s edge. She said nothing of the figure entered before the face and gave no figure for the dressed grain the arithmetic did not know the cost of. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 118 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 11, 12 and 13 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the word at the well was not brought under the roof as a teaching. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot and the fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest at the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found where put and stayed a finding (T097/T060/T086 advanced, not paid). \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a basket, a well and a going of the light are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due. She said nothing of the well-word, gave no figure to the cost of the dressed grain and left the crack showing; no new scar or possession, no change of voice. \textbf{Ch 117 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 8, 9 and 10 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the first Account-day of the year was not made a threshold or a door. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, moved her lips on a two-gapped row, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire, said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found where put on the mornings and goings of the light of all three days and stayed a finding, not a placing (T097/T060/T086 advanced, not paid). \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a basket, a market and a bed are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due on an Account-day. Before first grey on Ilmen 10 she carried him down, set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay, stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over the wicker. With Tarn nothing changed at the kindling; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper; with Berr no figure came into the house from the reading, and the figure read over the covered grain did not know what it cost. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession, no change of voice. \textbf{Ch 116 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 5, 6 and 7 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the new year’s first working week was kept as any working week. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw — on Ilmen 7, \emph{You’ll want more than that come the drying} — and turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, moved her lips on a two-gapped row, glanced once at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the hairline showed between old-brass staple and tighter wire with both proverbs to pot and fire, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful — \emph{Lie down. You’ll keep better there} — and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found where put on all three mornings and goings of the light and stayed a finding, not a placing (T097/T060/T086 advanced, not paid). \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf and a basket are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due on a tending day. Before first grey on Ilmen 6 three or more men unnamed went low into the room off the wheel-shed; she gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, and when a man from Slate Row whose name was on no roll stood at the yard’s edge with his hands loose she carried him down at the half-pace and went wide around the seven places and said no word to him, no loaf passing and no slate shown (T035/T031/T080 advanced, not paid). With Tarn the sixth piece at the kindling stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside the unforged collector sentence, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, the loan uncalled at the end of a term already ended and the head not turned toward the landing; with Jorra her unfinished sentence arrived at the pot through the bent finger standing in the cold damper, and the promise under the shed was neither given nor withdrawn. Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken 399, 400 and 401 days, the fire’s fifth unpaid the same number. No new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 115 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 2, 3 and 4 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer: the household went back to its grammar as though nothing had turned and the new year’s first arithmetic waited for Ilmen 10, unbrought. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stayed unread, moved her lips on a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the tighter wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and new binding and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration as a surgeon keeps a graft apart from a cure, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, and set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} the wool was found folded where put on the three mornings and at the three goings of the light, no third crust, name, gift, payment or payer. The widow’s mark hung untouched on all three days, a morning, a shelf, a bed and an afternoon being no openings; seven openings in seven months were seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due. On Ilmen 3 a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards and she shut her hand half over nothing beyond the pot board; a number rose out of a fist and went back into a sleeve; word came up that a runner had gone up the clay road with the writing turned to her sleeve and unread, and that the soft-cuffed clerk was still set at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge with his slate turned inward for a measure nobody called. With Tarn the sixth stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, the term ended and the loan uncalled, and his head went a degree toward the landing and back to the broom without a word; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper, one iron with two bites, and he came out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. Garl stayed in objects, his name unspoken 396, 397 and 398 days while the carried fire’s fifth went unpaid the same number, the two standing side by side without becoming one. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 114 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across the Remembering, the Last Day and Ilmen 1 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer: the Five ended with the Last Day and the year turned on Ilmen 1 with nothing signed, and the household went back to its grammar as though nothing had turned. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told it was the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread; lips on a two-gapped row unfigured; one glance at the clay jar under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire, never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} the wool was found folded where put on the three mornings and at the three goings of the light, no third crust, name, gift, payment or payer. On the Remembering she took the basket on an errand to House Silt three doors down, set it just inside the finger’s-width-open door at the edge of the light away from every open slate, took what she came for and went, neither naming the room nor making a lesson of the visit; the pewter tin above the empty bed was not opened. On the Last Day she baked bread and left the grey in the corners where no broom had gone in two years; a neighbour called it dealt with because it would be burnt in the morning and she did not say it, and she did not sweep the ridge early. On Ilmen 1 the yard burnt its grey and called it gone and she still said nothing. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a holy day, a baking and a burning of another yard’s grey are not openings, and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule with no eighth made due. With Tarn and Jorra she said nothing of the uncalled loan, the ended term or the ungiven promise; the carried fire’s fifth stayed unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken 393, 394 and 395 days. No change of voice, no new scar or possession; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 113 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Kindling, Weighing and the Long Night as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer: the three holy days kept their names, had no tend-days and no market, and the year was not said to turn on any of them. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread; lips on a two-gapped row unfigured; one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire, never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found folded where she put it on the fifteenth on the three mornings and at the three goings of the light, with no third crust, name, gift, payment or payer. On the Long Night she banked the fire early against the going of the light, told the coals it was the thaw where another woman would say I, turned them with the back of a broken pot, kept her finger above the charcoal and her lips on a two-gapped row, glanced once at the clay jar with her hand half over nothing, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful and set the pot rim two inches beyond his reach with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; later, sitting in the dark near the hearth with her hands in her lap and not still, counting the spoons on the pot board, the nails in the boards and the breaths of a child nobody has numbered, she put her fingers on the pot’s hairline a breath longer than any check required, took them away without making a sixth held object or writing a cause across it, and said low to the banked coals something about the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a holy day is not an opening and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule with no eighth made due. The year’s fire came up the Clay Yard in a clay dish from hearth to hearth before first light from a source nobody under the roof names or prices; the carried fire’s fifth stayed unpaid with Garl’s name unspoken 390, 391 and 392 days. On Kindling she carried the basket to the room two doors down and set him at the edge of the light where he could see and not join, standing half a pace off and giving no instruction to the basket; she said nothing of the room, the tube, the slate or the woman afterward. No new scar or possession and no change of voice; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 112 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 28, 29 and 30 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the year went out without a boundary drawn with neither of the district’s two habits of naming its months set right or left. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row unfigured; one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place and once and not twice, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found folded once where she put it on the fifteenth on the three mornings and at the three goings of the light, with no third crust, name, gift, payment or payer. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a yard, a market, a Cross, a going of the light and a bed are no openings — seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due. On Stone 30 she carried him down before first light, set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, giving no instruction or reason to the basket, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over the wicker. With Tarn and Jorra the equality held unremarked; with Ilva and Hessa nothing from the well or the road came under the roof as a figure; with Berr twelve arithmetics stood behind one unsigned figure and bought no teaching here; with Garl his name went unspoken 387, 388 and 389 days and the carried fire’s fifth stayed unpaid. No new scar or possession and no change of voice; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 111 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 25, 26 and 27 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the eleven readings and the fourth direction stood behind the household and bought no teaching here. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row figuring neither gap; one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place and once and not twice, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found folded once where she put it on the fifteenth on the tenth, eleventh and twelfth mornings and goings of the light, with no third crust, no name, no gift, no payment and no payer. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a rack, a yard, a going of the light and a bed are no openings — seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth is made due; the fire kept four low pulls with its fifth unpaid 384, 385 and 386 days. Ilva kept her ninth at the well on Stone 26; Tarn’s loan stayed uncalled at the very end of the seventh year and Jorra’s promise neither given nor withdrawn. No bond changed hands and no new scar or possession; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 110 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 22, 23 and 24 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the eleven readings and the fourth direction stood behind the household and bought no teaching here. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row figuring neither gap; one glance at the clay jar under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place and once and not twice, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold to the empty place; the wool was found folded once where she put it on the fifteenth on the seventh, eighth and ninth mornings and at the seventh, eighth and ninth goings of the light, with no third crust, no name, no gift, no payment and no payer. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a rack, a yard, a going of the light and a bed are no openings — seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth is made due. With Tarn the exact account held at six counted and the seventh at the lip with the loan uncalled at the very end of the seventh year; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper, one iron with two bites, and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not made a second time; with Ilva the ninth stayed nine at the well on Stone 22 and with Hessa the slate went up unread on Stone 23. Nothing from the fourth direction over the boards came under the roof as lesson or payment. No new scar or possession, no change of voice; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 109 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 19, 20 and 21 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the eleventh arithmetic stood behind the household and bought no teaching here, and she did not join the keeping at the fold to anything read at the Cross. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told it was the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row figured neither way; one glance at the clay jar under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping was tested again and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the wool was found folded once where she put it on the fifteenth on the fourth, fifth and sixth mornings and at the fourth, fifth and sixth goings of the light, with no third crust, no name, no gift, no payment and no payer. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a yard, a market, a Cross, a going of the light and a bed are no openings — seven openings in seven months seven and not a rule and no eighth made due. On Stone 20 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay, stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over him. With Tarn and Jorra the exact household account held, the knife-sill and the damper’s two bites unremarked; Garl’s name was unspoken and the fire’s fifth unpaid three hundred and seventy-eight, seventy-nine and eighty days. No new scar or possession, no change of voice; she has still not said whose child he is.

\textbf{Ch 108 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 16, 17 and 18 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the Drawing and the ten arithmetics brought no teaching here. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row unfigured; one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she banked against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. \textbf{The keeping was tested and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} her hand put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold to the empty place; the wool was found folded once where she put it on the fifteenth on all three mornings and at all three goings of the light, with no third crust, no name, no gift, no payment and no payer. With Tarn the exact account held at six counted and the seventh at the lip with the loan uncalled; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper, one iron with two bites, and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not made a second time. Ilva at the well on the sixteenth and Hessa going up the road on the seventeenth brought no figure under this roof; Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken 375, 376 and 377 days. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid.

\textbf{Ch 107 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 13, 14 and 15 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; the Hearth Drawing stood behind the household with no lesson made of it and the tenth arithmetic went up the clay road in Berr’s box and bought no teaching here. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread; lips on a two-gapped row figuring neither gap; one glance at the clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft. On the mornings of the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth the empty place beside the crust was left exactly as it had been — no hand at it, no third, no name — so that what she did at the going of the light on the fifteenth would be a change and not a habit. \textbf{The chapter’s one change, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} at the going of the light on the fifteenth, setting him on his bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf and putting the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, her hand did what hands do at a bed and tucked the wool into the empty place beside the crust — not to fill the place, which kept its shape and its emptiness both, but to leave the warmth of a hand where the cold had been. No word went with it, no third crust was put there, no name was spoken over the place, no look was given toward his face and no instruction to the basket; her hand rested the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away and the thread was left frozen and unwiped. The boy filed it on a place of its own and made no gift, payment, joining or rule of it. With Tarn the exact account held at six counted and the seventh at the lip, the loan uncalled; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper, one iron with two bites, and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not made a second time. Ilva at the well on the thirteenth and Hessa coming down the road on the fourteenth brought no figure under this roof; Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken 372, 373 and 374 days. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid.

\textbf{Ch 106 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road on Stone 10, 11 or 12 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, the half-pace from every open slate, the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number and widest around the returning-line place, the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with its hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, the dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful, the charcoal unread beneath her finger, lips on a two-gapped row figured neither way, one glance at the clay jar and the hand shut half over nothing, the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. On Stone 10 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, carrying him home at the going of the light saying nothing. On Stone 12 she carried him two doors down to the Drawing, set him at the edge of the light where he could see and not join and stood half a pace off through the whole collection, saying nothing to the basket; the widow’s mark stayed untouched because a Drawing is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. At the going of the light she carried him home, said nothing of the room, the tube, the child or the cup, righted the fold without a look at his face and let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed. With Tarn the exact account held, six counted where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the loan uncalled; with Jorra the men unnamed went low into the back room and his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of her unfinished sentence, one iron with two bites, and came out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; Garl’s name stayed unspoken 369, 370 and 371 days, his debt uncalled and worse for being uncalled. Dessa stayed dead, Alda’s writing unasked about, Hessa’s slate unread and Ilva’s strip in her sleeve. No bond paid, sold, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 105 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 7, 8 and 9 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the day a year before when he was born came round on Stone 7 and went as an ordinary tending day: no party, cake, figure, recognition or threshold, no loaf set aside and no word said over the basket, and neither of the district’s two habits of naming the months set right or left. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, her lips on a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and no handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped, saying nothing of where they had been. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on Stone 7, 8 or 9} — seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth was made due; the not-going on the birthday was not a slight, a mercy or an answer to a question nobody put, and nothing under any roof altered by one mark on account of a year finished. With Tarn the six and the seventh and the checked keepings held unremarked; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not left a second time; with Garl the objects kept the house in his shape and his name went unspoken 366, 367 and 368 days, the carried fire’s fifth unpaid the same number. Nine arithmetics stood behind one unsigned figure, the river’s winter skin stayed found where put and was not spent on the birthday, this day or the Drawing. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 104 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 4, 5 and 6 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the first firing of Stone went behind the household without a lesson anybody named. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{Her one change, T058/T079 advanced and not paid:} on the morning of Stone 5, before any instruction went to the basket, she carried him to the kiln mouth and set him level out of the draught where the heat came to him sideways, stood over him with her hands gone still, put her left hand to the widow’s mark at her throat for one breath and let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under a broken pot. The fire took, answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and sixty-four days; nobody praised the opening, named what it mended, entered a slate or made a lesson of it. Seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule, the sixth stands behind at Ash 2 without a name and no eighth is made due; she did not touch the mark again at shelf, well, rack, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, going of light or bed. With Tarn the six and the seventh and the checked objects held; with Jorra the unfinished sentence still reached the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not left a second time; with Ilva the ninth hand at the well on Stone 4 stayed nine; with Garl the objects held and his name went unspoken three hundred and sixty-three, sixty-four and sixty-five days. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 103 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Stone 1, 2 and 3 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the river’s winter skin bought no opening here. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number and widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, an afternoon, a going of the light and a bed are not openings — six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due. The river’s note came low under its skin through the finger’s-width door and she made nothing of it. With Tarn the six and the seventh, the checked breath and thumb’s resting and the uncalled loan went unremarked; with Jorra the dust, the withheld note and the bent finger standing ahead of her unfinished sentence went unasked about and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not made a second time; with Ilva at the well on Stone 2 the count stayed in wood and the question put was answered; with Garl the objects kept his shape and his name went unspoken 360, 361 and 362 days. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 102 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment across Ash 28, 29 and 30. She kept the hearth grammar at both ends of every day — fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with a broken pot’s back, \emph{The house will keep it}, intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, charcoal unread beneath her finger, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs and the hairline showing, dressed grain turned under wool with no figure or handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him at the half-pace, went wide around the seven places, set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft and left the thread where it lay; on Ash 30 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade, stood half a pace off and carried him home saying nothing of what had been read over the wicker. The widow’s mark hung where it hung and was not a hand’s business on any of the three days. With Tarn the six and the seventh, the knife at the sill, the checked breath and thumb’s resting and the uncalled loan went unremarked; with Jorra the dust, the withheld note and the bent finger standing ahead of her unfinished sentence went unasked about and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not made a second time; with Berr her basket sat in his shade while his figure went twice over it and his third subtraction went up the road locked and unread; with Hessa and Ilva nothing came from the road or the well as a figure under this roof. Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken three hundred and fifty-seven, fifty-eight and fifty-nine days and his tile debt uncalled. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 101 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 25, 26 and 27, and nothing from the yard, the well or the directions went under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing between the old-brass staple and the tighter wire, dressed grain turned under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful, and the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, and at each going of the light set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — the last touch was at the kiln mouth on Ash 2 — six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due; a morning, a hearth, a going of the light and a bed are not openings. With Tarn the six and the seventh held unremarked, and the Bone 26 thumb’s resting and the Ash 14 held breath were checked on the twenty-fifth, twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh, found where put and not made again, with no word from her and no lesson under the roof. With Jorra Sella’s unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot: on Ash 26 and 27 his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of her words, took the cold out of the fingertip, moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and was left standing, and on the twenty-sixth, after the work was done and the household straightened around the waiting, it stayed a breath longer than the work required; she asked nothing about it, gave it no name and made no opening, payment or lesson of it under the roof (T062/T035/T031 and T061/T082 advanced, not paid). At the well on Ash 26 Ilva kept her count in wood and answered the question put, and nothing came from that well under the roof as figure, cause or payment (T080 advanced, not paid). Eight arithmetics stood behind one unsigned figure with both Ash subtractions locked in Berr’s box and the figure read still not the figure paid; Garl’s name was unspoken 354, 355 and 356 days with his fifth pull unpaid the same number. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid. Forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 99 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 19, 20 and 21, and nothing from the Cross, the yard or the reading went under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, lips on a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire, dressed grain turned once under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, and at each going of the light set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — the last touch was at the kiln mouth on Ash 2 — six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due. On Ash 20, the dark month’s second Account-day and market, she carried him down before first light, set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of where they had been or what had been read over him. Berr called the levy and denied it with \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never I, and went off up the road with the box locked and Ash’s second true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; \textbf{eight arithmetics now stand behind one printed figure, eight are eight and not one account}, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space, and she gave none of it a lesson under the roof. With Tarn the six and the seventh held unremarked, and the Ash 14 held breath at the knife-sill was checked on the nineteenth, twentieth and twenty-first and not made again; with Jorra the dusty forearms, the withheld note and the bent finger standing in the cold damper ahead of her unfinished sentence went unasked about; with Ilva at the well on Ash 19 nothing came from the strip in the sleeve, and no figure came off the wood. Hessa took the slate up the road unread and no runner came on the other two days. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 348, 349 and 350 days and his tile debt uncalled. No new scar or possession, no bond changed hands and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 98 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 16, 17 and 18, and nothing from the yard, the well or the ownerless voice crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, dressed grain turned once under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, and at each going of the light set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. The widow’s mark hung where it hung on all three days, untouched since the kiln mouth on Ash 2; six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due, and the word that went up the terrace bought no opening here. With Tarn the six and the seventh held unremarked, and the Ash 14 held breath at the knife-sill was checked on the sixteenth, seventeenth and eighteenth, found where it had been put and not made again, with no word from her and no lesson under the roof. With Jorra the dusty forearms, the withheld note and the bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about; when the ownerless direction went around the boards he grew quieter and the household straightened around the quiet without an order from anybody, and she gave the fire its instruction and went on. With Ilva at the well on Ash 17 nothing came from the strip in the sleeve; with Berr and Hessa nothing came up the clay road and no runner was seen. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 345, 346 and 347 days and the tile debt uncalled. No new scar or possession, no bond changed hands and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 97 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 13, 14 and 15 and nothing crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, dressed grain turned under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, and at each going of the light set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. The widow’s mark hung where it hung on all three days, untouched since the kiln mouth on Ash 2; six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due. With Tarn the six and the seventh held unremarked, and the held breath he left at the knife-sill on Ash 14 was not named, joined or made a lesson of under the roof; with Jorra the dusty forearms, the withheld note and the bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about and the shed kept its silence; with Ilva at the well on Ash 15 the count stayed in wood and the question put was answered; with Berr and Hessa nothing came up the clay road in these three days. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 342, 343 and 344 days, the pot-crack resting beside the five objects and expressly not a sixth, and the tile debt neither paid nor settled. Repair stayed apart from restoration; no new scar or possession, no bond changed hands and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 96 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 10, 11 and 12 and nothing from the Cross crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Fire before basket at both ends of every day, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, small intake and hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs to pot and fire and the crack left showing, dressed grain turned under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. On Ash 10 she carried him down before first light at the half-pace she keeps from every open slate, set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of where they had been or what had been read over the basket; on Ash 11 and 12 there was no market, Cross or bell. The widow’s mark hung where it hung and was not touched on any of the three days, the last touch having been at the kiln mouth on Ash 2; six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due. With Berr the figure went twice over the basket and he denied the levy with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and said something low to the block about kindness being entered; with Hessa the slate went up the road unread, her hand to it before her eyes to the crowd; with Ilva at the well on Ash 11 the count stayed in wood and the question put was answered; with Tarn the six and the seventh held and his thumb’s resting was checked and not made again; with Jorra the bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of an unfinished sentence and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed with the promise neither given nor withdrawn. Garl’s name was unspoken 339, 340 and 341 days and his tile debt uncalled. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 95 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands through Ash 7, 8 and 9, and the chapter’s one movement was hers and was not spent. She went to the fire before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, turned the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, went wide around the seven walked-around places, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire and the pot and never to the basket, and at the going of the light on Ash 9 set him on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The one change, advanced and not paid (T009/T013/T092, T060/T086):} at the going of the light on Ash 9 her thumb arrived at the wire where it crossed the crack of the twice-mended pot and stayed one breath longer than the lift had need of before she let the weight come on the handle, the hairline of the original break left showing between the old-brass staple and the tighter wire. She said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, and made no announcement, figure or lesson of the interval. The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days; six openings in six months were six and not a rule and no seventh was made due. With Tarn the six and the seventh held unremarked; with Jorra the bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of her unfinished sentence on Ash 9 and the household straightened around the quiet without an order; Ilva’s ninth hand at the well on Ash 8 brought no figure under the roof. Garl’s name was unspoken three hundred and thirty-six, thirty-seven and thirty-eight days and his debt stayed uncalled. No bond was paid or spoken, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 94 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands across Ash 4–6 and no collector came up or down the clay road. She went to the fire before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, turning the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and lifting no handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, instruction always to the wool, the fire and the pot and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number; the three coverings stayed weather entered nowhere and the dressed grain stayed covered and unfigured. At the going of the light on Ash 6 she set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, left the thread where it lay and said nothing of where they had been. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a morning, a hearth, a going of the light and a bed are not openings — and the sixth opening at the kiln mouth on Ash 2 was not revisited as sign, lesson, mending or payment and no seventh was made due. When an ownerless voice over the boards on Ash 5 joined the burned slate to the room with the damper shut she told the fire it was the thaw and gave the voice no name and the saying no figure; she has lost a husband to that danger and has never described it that way herself. With Tarn the exact account of six and the seventh went unremarked; with Jorra the dust, the wheel first, the withheld note and the bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about, and his quieter silence after the joining got no order from her. Ilva’s strip stayed in her sleeve and Hessa’s slate went down the road unread; nothing from either crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and no lesson was made of any of it.

\textbf{Ch 93 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands across Ash 1–3, and the one change was hers and was put behind the household without a name. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, turned them with the back of a broken pot, stood a moment counting a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, leaving the crack showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and lifted no handful, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, righted the fold at ear and chin without a look at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The one change, advanced and not paid (T058/T079, T088):} on Ash 2, the dark month’s first firing, she carried the basket to the kiln mouth and set it level out of the draught where the heat came to him sideways and not full; before any instruction went to the basket and before any word she stood over him with her hands still, put her left hand to the widow’s mark at her throat — the cord oiled where a working thumb had touched it ten thousand times, the little-door burn on the back of her left hand half-closing on the cord — held it one breath and let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot. The fire took, still answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and thirty-one days. Six openings in six months are six and not a rule; nobody praised the opening, named what it mended, entered a slate or made a lesson of it, the five behind were not looked at again as signs or payments, and no seventh was made due. She did not touch the mark again at shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, dusk or going of the light, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. On all three days her fingers at the rack end went in and came out without closing; the handful of Bone 22 stayed one object and was not made again. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the river wind and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number; the three coverings stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair, and the month’s hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures. At the going of the light on Ash 3 she set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, left the thread where it lay, and said nothing of where they had been. With Tarn the exact account of six and the seventh went unremarked and his \emph{Yes, house} to an early and a late thaw got no answer from her; with Jorra the unnamed back-room men, the dust and the bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about and his quieter silence at the burned-slate saying got no instruction from her. Ilva came once to the well on Ash 2 with her strip unread and the ninth hand nine; nothing from that well crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. Garl’s name was unspoken three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days and his tile debt stayed uncalled; the twice-mended pot’s crack showed and repair stayed apart from restoration. She wants the house kept as it is kept, with no figure spoken over what it does. No bond changed hands, no tin or box was opened, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 92 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands across Bone 28–30. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person and left the crack showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and lifted no handful, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, righted the fold at ear and chin without a look at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped, and touched the widow’s mark at no hour because a morning, a hearth, a rack, a well, a yard, a market, a Cross and a bed are not openings and five openings in five months are five and not a rule. On all three days her fingers at the rack end went in and came out and did not close on the grain; the handful of Bone 22 stayed one object and was not made again. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number; the stayed frost gone off the north lip, the skinned trough and the silt-clouded plate on its flat stone stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair, and the month’s hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures. On Bone 30, the month’s third and last Account-day and market, she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr’s twice-read figure and the bell, giving no instruction or reason to the basket, and carried him home at the going of the light. In the small hours she set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, righted the fold at his ear without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, and left the thread where it lay; a small scrape of a foot on the loft stair came from above and behind earlier, with no interior entered. She said nothing of where they had been or what had been read over the basket. Nobody under any roof spoke a number or a name to the basket. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice; she wants the house kept as it is kept, with no figure spoken over what it does.

\textbf{Ch 91 (bonds).} With Corin nothing changed hands across Bone 25–27.
